jfczvpss.c: Collection of notes on medicine, followed by medical receipts, etc.: in English. Rough pen-drawing of the geocentric Cosmos on verso of first leaf: on ll. 41-53 crude illustrations of urine flasks, some partly coloured. The first 55 ll. contain notes on medical astrology, urines, etc. The remainder of the volume consists of medical receipts and remedies, mostly by the same hand. In the lower margin of l. 182 'Gerard Jaques his book'. In this inscription the name 'John' which was apparently written first, has been struck through, and 'Gerard' written above it. On fol. 45v some scribblings including 'Ger. Jaques', 'James Jaques his booke': in the latter the name 'James' has perhaps been altered to 'John'.

jffrewmh.c: A 19th century cookery book with 67 pages of recipes, listed on the front page and a loose sheet of paper for 'Recipe to preserve French Beans.' At the back of the book there are 21 pages of medical and domestic recipes.

jjeqy95a.c: Collection of medical, including a few veterinary, receipts, with cookery and household receipts. This MS. is mainly written by two more or less contemporary hands. Most of the cookery receipts are in the first section (130 ff.); the second section begins from the other end of the volume; each section has its own index. The collection was perhaps made by a member of the Lambton family, who certainly seems to have been the writer of the more literate hand. Fol. 16v. A receipt for the ague. Signed 'C. L.'; 17v. For a vomit. 'By Edward Lambton'; 120. Orange brandy. 'F. [?] Lambton'; 125. To make lemmon water. 'A. Lambton'. In the second section are several veterinary receipts 'By Doctor Edward Lambton', and the note, 'From my Brother Edward Lambton this 24th November 1750'.

jjfyhdhj.c: Collection of medical, household and cookery recipes, many taken from printed sources. The entries are in two hands, an earlier (pp. 4-16), and a later one (17-107); one of the earlier recipes is taken from the Penny Magazine of 7 July 1838 (p. 13); some of the later ones are derived from newspapers of the period 1847-49, including the Manchester Guardian and Liverpool Echo (pp. 28, 34-35), and several press cuttings relating to recipes and other medical subjects have been stuck into the volume. There is a short section on baths (pp. 38-42). The later hand apparently continued to add to the collection until the end of the century. Internal evidence suggests this later compiler may have been surnamed Guest and been resident in south-west Lancashire.

jqa8q7cz.t: English Recipe Book, 17th century - early 18th century.
jqa8q7cz.c: Collection of medical, culinary and household recipes, in various hands. The earliest recipes are in a single mid-17th century hand, and are arranged in four sections, entitled 'Physicall Receites' (ff. 2-44), 'Excellent Receites for Chirurgery' (ff. 45-89), Receites of Curiosity' (ff. 90-133) and 'Receites of good Huswifrye' (ff. 134-177). Later entries have been added throughout the book, the latest in a hand that includes the date 21 September 1710 against a recipe for elder wine (f. 121). This hand is apparently the same as that responsible for various jottings on f. 178v., including the names 'Jos. Beachcroft', 'James Pickering' and 'James Astry'. Authorities include 'Doctor Staples (f. 12v.), 'Dr Burgis', 'Dr Avery' (f. 14v.), 'Dr Prys' (f. 21v.), and several relatives ('Cossen Hartnell, f. 12v., 'Sister Collier', f. 19v., 'Aunt Walker', ff. 51-52).

kug2qkry.c: Manuscript recipe book of Anna-Maria Meysey, containing culinary, domestic and medical receipts. The volume is written in one hand and compiles family recipes for baked goods, meat, medical remedies and domestic chores including cures for rheumatism and inflamed eyes, recipes for cakes and meat stews and how to wash silk stockings. The book attributes these recipes to various family and friends, including Mrs Wodhull of Thenford (providing recipes for Beef Tea, Lemonade, Orangeade, 'Doctor Lowers Cholic Tincture', and 'For cleaning mahogany tables', among others), Mrs Meysey of Worcester ('To pickle Mangoes'), Sister Turton ('Trentham Cheese' and 'To make Tar Water'), Aunt Meysey Shakenhurst ('To bottle gooseberry's', and 'To make puff Past') and E. Turton (Tooth Powder). In several instances notes that the recipe is copied from an outside source e.g. Thomson Family Herbal by Bewick. The volume also features an index of recipes towards the end of the volume.

kx9c362k.c: English medical practitioner's notebook containing pharmaceutical recipes, with some case histories, and a few medical charms. The main component of the text (ff. 1-54) is a suite of recipes in an early 18th century hand, organised for the most part alphabetically by disease or symptom. A later hand or hands have added additional recipes and other matter, including prices against some of the cures. The medical charms (ff. 33v-35) are in the same early 18th century hand. The remainder of the text (f. 56 onwards) comprises later recipes and case histories in the same later hand or hands noted above, with the addition of a Latin charm on the final leaf.

kxysf95h.c: Artznei-buch. The first 8 ll. contain entries in a later 16th cent. hand. On fol. 57, the Author has signed and dated 1537 a receipt for 'Aurum potabile': and inside the upper cover is a receipt for a dye ending 'probatum durch mich hans frey 1549'. Below is a coat of arms blazoned in water-colour, perhaps that of the Compiler.

kz3p9d6f.c: Hospital doctor's pocketbook, numerous detailed cases. The volume was purchased from a Dublin stationer's and the patients' addresses suggest that the hospital itself was in Dublin.

Most of fol. 22v and fol. 23 are written in a late 16th or early 17th cent. hand, which is also found in the additions to MS. No. 378 mentioned above. On fol. 22 a receipt for 'Unguentum gratia dei' has been interpolated into the text, which continues on line 4 from the last line of fol. 21v. On the verso of the first leaf is written 'Beschryben durch mich hanns fridrich Wallin vogt zu falckenstein. Anno 1587'. The original work seems to end on the 45th leaf. It is followed by a number of medical and veterinary receipts in German, by various 17th and 18th cent. hands. The first 4 leaves contain plague remedies. On the last leaf is the signature of 'Johann Victor Antoni Blutz der grossennrathi', by an 18th cent. hand. Produced in Falkenstein.

m36jrrsj.c: A paper manuscript copy of the Circa instans attributed to Platearius, without illustrations, written possibly in Germany in the 1440s-1450s.Contents:ff. 1r-69r: Circa instans or Liber de simplici medicina, in Latin, a late 12th-century pharmacopoeial and therapeutic compilation attributed to a physician operating in the milieu of the School of Salerno, known under the name of Platearius. The text in the present manuscript is identifiable with the first version of variant B (versio B) of the Circa instans, including between 250 and 277 chapters and testified in approximately 133 manuscripts produced between the last decades of the 12th and the late 15th century: I. Ventura, 'Il Circa instans attribuito a Platearius: trasmissione manoscritta, redazioni, criteri di costruzione di un'edizione critica', Revue d'histoire des textes, 10 (2015), pp. 251-362 (in particular pp. 261-6; with mention of the present manuscript on pp. 265, 302, 337); eadem, 'Un best-seller farmaceutico medioevale tra produzione di libri e pratiche di lettura: il Circa instans attribuito a Platearius', in Orbis disciplinae. Hommages en l'honneur de Patrick Gautier Dalch?, ed. N. Bouloux, A. Dan and G. Tolias (Tur

m47vxt6m.c: Lettered outside the upper cover in ink 'Of Discerning of Men. Tomus primus [?]'. The MS. is a work on physiognomy in tabular form, and appears to be an English version of the 'Tabulae physiognomonicae' by Dominicus de Rubeis, published at Venice in 1639.

m68zhzp2.c: Les vraies Clavicules du Roy Salomon avec les Pentacules et Talismans dont il se servat journellement. Livre des nombres sacr?s. Illustrated with pen-drawn magical figures, sigils, etc.

Leaf 4 and 5r contain 'Von dem lebendigen wasser daz man da nennet daz guldin wasser hat gelert der...Meister Bartholomeus von franckfort'. Ll. 13-end contain the Glossary of Herbs beginning: 'Artimesia significat bibosz' which is entered in Thorndike's 'Incipits' Col. 63, and attributed to 'Macer'.

mcjcx99m.t: A translated extract of Avicenna's Canon of Medicine. The persian translation can be seen interlinear with the Arabic until folio 19b. Leaves missing at the end.
mcjcx99m.c: A translated extract of Avicenna's Canon of Medicine. The persian translation can be seen interlinear with the Arabic until folio 19b. Leaves missing at the end.

mcnvc4x2.c: Collection of medical, veterinary, household and technical receipts. The name of G. Cownley is written inside the upper cover.

mcnw8amm.c: Recueil de quelques receptes trez ?prouv?es. Lettered on spine 'Les secrets de Mr. Ageron.' Pp. 150-173 contain 'Dissertation chymique adress?e aux sublimes investigateurs et partisans de la Nature', concerning the making of 'or potable'. Pp. 174-207-Methods of dyeing.

mctc2q63.c: "Mrs. Elizabeth Hirst her book." A collection of medical and cookery receipts: in English, with additions by contemporary and early 18th cent. hands. pp. 1-92, "Chirurgery and physicall receipts"; 93-211, "Choice receipts for cookery"; 218-end, "Choyce receits for wines and sweet meates." The receipts are arranged in alphabetical order: all after letter Q of the last section is wanting. On the first leaf 'Mrs. Elizabeth Hirst her book. 1684'.

mdf76qcb.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few medical and household receipts. Written by the same hand as far as p. 211, with a few additions by several hands [c. 1850]: there is an elaborate index, and the latest dated entry is 1834 on p. 204. A small paper-covered note-book, with 13 separate receipts for cookery and medical remedies, by various hands. Those in the notebook, perhaps written c. 1810, have been copied into the larger volume. Among these loose receipts, etc. is a letter dated 14 July, 1898 from H. M. Gilbert & Sons of Southampton, which refers to this MS.: 'We are sending...a M.S. book of recipes which we purchased yesterday and which we think you will like to have. It came from a good old family (an Admiral's)....' This letter is addressed to Francis G. Smart Esq., who is probably Dr. Francis Gray Smart of Tunbridge Wells, who died there in 1913.

mdfn7hqp.t: von Sacher-Masoch, Leopold (1836 - 1895) and von Sacher-Masoch, Aurora (1846 - post-1906).
mdfn7hqp.c: Letters and postcards from Leopold von Sacher-Masoch, Austrian novelist and source of the term 'masochist', to fellow-writers Otto von Kapff (b. 1855) and his wife Franziska von Kapff-Essenther (1843-1899). With additional letters from Aurora von Sacher-Masoch [n?e von R?melin, pseudonym Wanda von Dunajew], and Hulda Meister (1856-1918), first and second wives of Leopold von Sacher-Masoch, and some associated papers. Largely on family and literary matters; von Kapff was Sacher-Masoch's private secretary after 1877.Summary List1-66Letters, postcards and 1 undated visiting card from Leopold von Sacher-Masoch and 1 letter (40) from Hulda Meister to Otto von Kapff, 1876-94.67-73Letters and postcards from Leopold von Sacher-Masoch to Franziska von Kapff-Essenther, 1881-82.74-76Miscellaneous papers from Leopold von Sacher-Masoch, 1865, 1877 and n.d.77-95Letters from Aurora von Sacher-Masoch to Otto von Kapff, 1880-81 and n.d.96-97Letters from Aurora von Sacher-Masoch to Franziska von Kapff-Essenther, 1881-82.98Letters from Aurora von Sacher-Masoch to her child Demetrius (Mitschi).

mejce2xx.t: Pseudo-Antonius Musa, De herba vettonica liber; Pseudo-Apuleius Platonicus, Herbarium or De medicaminibus herbarum liber, imperfect.
mejce2xx.c: An illustrated herbal describing the healing properties of plants, including a short text on the properties of the herb betony, traditionally attributed to Antonius Musa, and a compilation of herbal remedies drawing from Greek and Latin sources, traditionally attributed to Apuleius Madaurensis or Apuleius Platonis. On paper, produced in Northern Italy, early 15th century. The manuscript is incomplete and its texts are out of sequence.Contents:1. ff. 1v-2v and 16r-v: Pseudo-Antonius Musa, De herba vettonica liber, a short treatise on the virtues and properties of the herb betony, imperfect. Traditionally attributed to Antonius Musa, the physician of Emperor Octavianus Augustus, it is in fact of unknown origin and dates to the 4th or 5th century AD: see M. Collins, Medieval Herbals: The Illustrative Traditions (Toronto: University of Toronto Press, 2000), p. 166.First printed without the prologue at the beginning of the Herbarium Apulei, as its first plant, by Johannes Philippus de Lignamine in Rome about 1481-82 (ISTC ih00058000), with woodblock engraving. Listed in eTK, A digital resource based on Lynn Thorndike and Pearl Kibre, A Catalogue of Incipits of Medieval Scientific Writin

mfpa8as6.c: Collection of medical receipts in German and Latin. At the end of the text (fol. 44) 'Geschriben durch Wolffen Ris'. On fol. 23 a receipt is headed: 'Jacob Thurner unnser haubtman zwo Saltzburg hat uns das Recept geben und soll gut und bew?rt sein fur das griess...' Many of the receipts are against plague. Produced in [Salzburg?]. A 'Register' or list of contents is included on fol. 44v-46r, with one further receipt on fol. 46v.

mgxcve5e.c: Medical compendium, containing receipts, notes on practical treatment, uroscopy, pregnancy, etc., also on astronomy, medical astrology, etc.: c.1530. With additions by later hands, of which many are by Henry Fowler, Rector of Minchinhampton (Glos.) dated between 1602 and 1641. Written partly in Latin and partly in English. Fowler has illustrated some of his entries with small pen-drawings, some anatomical, grotesque heads, animals, etc. and flowers-the latter perhaps as a rebus for his name. Contents: Ff. 1-10 On urines, signs of pregnancy, visitatio infirmi, diet, etc. In Latin. 11-179 List of diseases and cures in alphabetical order by Spinney; mainly in English, but some entries in Latin. 180-187 On astronomy, medical astrology, etc. In Latin. 189-200 Bloodletting, the four Humours, physiological notes, purgatives, uroscopy, etc. In Latin. Among the above are interspersed receipts and notes in English and Latin by several Elizabethan hands. Fol. 119v contains the beginning only of 'The testamente and Laste will of Wylliame tracye esquire', in English and written out by Spinney. mjn2b2gj.c: Collection of medical, cookery and other receipts: with entries by other hands. The date 1844 is found on the first leaf of the cookery section at the other end of the volume: the latest date in the medical section is 1865. On the verso of the fifth leaf of this section is a note 'Taken by L.N.W. from "The Record", June 16, 1847': in the cookery section there are receipts stated to be copied by Anne White.

mmd58kev.c: Receptes pour les chevaus Recueil de secrets et curiosit?s. The 'Recueil' begins at the other end of the volume. The compiler's name is written in the upper margin of the first page of the 'Table des Receptes pour les chevaus'.

mmr25adm.c: Ein neu Buch von der Ross Artzney darin allerhand statliche Experiment und Artzneien wie die in Turk?y, Ungarn, und Niederlanden, auch an Etlichen Vornehmen Teutschen, Chur-und Firstlichen H?fen ... gesamlet, auch ... mit warten und pflegen der Rosse als auch allerhandt deroselben Krankheiten und gebrechen ... von Zauberey Experimentiert und vielfaltig bewahrt worden. The author was 'Rossarzt' to the Court of Brandenburg after some years of military service in Central Europe. He first published the work in Berlin in 1618 and there were later editions down to 1710. [Cf. Chiodi (V.) Storia veterinaria, Milan. 1957, pp. 232, 233].

mn77q3mq.c: Collection of medical receipts in German, including a 'Regiment in Zeit der Pestilentz'. At the end a 'Consilium' in Latin 'De catarrho cerebri et curatione ejusdem'. The Plague tract has not been identified, and is in the form of a prayer.

mnr8hubd.t: A manuscript of commentary on Najib al-Samarqandi's famous medical manuscript "Causes and symptoms."
mnr8hubd.c: A manuscript of commentary on Najib al-Samarqandi's famous medical manuscript "Causes and symptoms."

mp934hn4.c: A collection of carefully executed water-colour drawings of symbolic alchemical illustrations, and of alchemical apparatus: including also portraits of Hermes, Geber, Aristotle, and two other unnamed 'Philosophers'. The Latin text gives a summary of alchemical doctrine in explanation of the illustrations: at the end are 'Versus universales' beginning: 'VIinum [sic] si summas [sic] cum solo corpore ponas' and ending (line 27): 'Versiculi scripta reserua philosophica dicta'. These are followed by 50 numbered alchemical Aphorisms, and some others. Finally, a further poem of 24 lines, beginning: 'Os et res nostros perficiat diuina Maestas', and ending: 'Sic uerbis scripti ficta referunt philosophorum dicta'.

mpp4q764.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few medical receipts: by several hands.

mpt6pyks.c: Doctrina illuminans: dasz ist das Liecht aller Lichter, oder die Lehr Winandi welche von Anstaig bisz zum Endte fideliter, parabolice tamen zum Chimischen Arbeith verleichtet... Illustrated with 19 water-colour symbolic drawings (ff. 25v-34v), in the first section, and 7 pen-drawings of alchemical furnaces, etc. in the last section (ff. 23-28). The first section (6 ll.) is headed: 'Von der weissen und klugen Mercurio'. The heading of the next section (40 ff.) is: 'Incipit Liber de Chimia In [gold] em et [silver] am'. On fol. 14 is a heading: 'Das Buch ist genandt das Liecht aller Liechter und die Lehr Winandi', and begins: 'Ich Winandus von rothen schild ain arzt...' It seems to end on fol. 15v, line 19: 'Dasz ist dasz Endt des heraufgeschribnen Werkhs', and is followed by extracts on Alchemy including quotations from the 'Turba Philosophorum', as far as fol. 25. Ff. 25v-35 contain 19 symbolic illustrations in the shape of flasks with descriptive text, showing the processes of the Stone. mru9zq82.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with some medical and household receipts. By several hands. With indented alphabet.

mry7kjjg.c: Recipes, etc. collected by a member of the Cooke Family. The title given above is that written on a label pasted down on the outside of the upper cover. The MS. however contains entries by various hands of medical, cookery and other receipts, including an extract from the 'Dispensatory of the Royal College of Physicians of London, 5th edition, 1773'. This section is dated 1782.

mrzjtwcx.t: Collection of medical receipts in English and Latin (Leech-Books, IV).

Item. Tak the rote of the rede dokke ... f. 7r [For the ston] ... or tak and drink sed of spurge tempered with wyn or ale.2. ff. 7v-10v Medical receipts in Latinf. 7v [C]ontra cancrum probatissimum experimentum accipe absinthium ... f. 10v [Ad faciendas margaritas] ... et purifica eas et sicut [?] ut margaritas.3. ff. 11r-61r Medical receipts in English and Latinf. 11r Theise ben the veynes to leten onne a man blod. for diuerse eueles. mtuh5xsb.c: Written in a rounded gothic hand, probably in England, 29 lines to a page. A few initials, paragraph marks and headings in red. Fol 1 Quoniam quidem ut in rethoricis tullius ['omne' superscribed] inquit expetendum... 'v, line 1 (Text begins) Capillus ex fumo grosso... 120v, line 25 ...ad idem valent. Conclee marine incense/cum olio rosato multum valent/Explicit VIATICVS. The fly-leaves, two at each end of which one is pasted down in to each cover, are folio leaves (cut down) from a 14th cent. MS. This has not been identified but it appears to be from a work on the Monastic Constitution of Evesham. It is written in double columns of 31 lines, with extensive marginal glosses by contemporary and later hands. There are initials in alternate red and blue, and blue and red. Above the text on fol. 1, a 16th cent. hand has written 'Constantini Affricani Monast[erii] Casanensis Viaticum. Agit de morbis et eorum signis et remediis'. The paper is water-marked with a variant of Briquet's Nos. 11667-11674, which date mostly from the second half of the 14th century.

mu5b8adg.t: The Arabic translation of Galen's Commentary on Hippocratic Epidemics.
mu5b8adg.c: The Arabic translation of Galen's Commentary on Hippocratic Epidemics.

muaguk8f.d: Undated. Estimated to be from 18th century A.D
muaguk8f.c: Two medical manuscripts in a composite volume. There is a statement on folio 30 that 8 out of the 42 chapters in the first manuscript by ibn Butlan are lacking. There is an index of contents for thirty four chapters.

mug5vsuq.c: Collection of cookery receipts, and a few medical and household receipts: with additional entries by several later hands. The medical receipts are found on the 17 ll. beginning from the other end of the volume. A number of cookery, household and medical receipts by various hands have been inserted loose. Inscribed inside the upper cover of this MS. is 'Mrs. Sheppard. Keyford House': the first receipt is dated 1818.

mv5xn43z.t: Receuil de plusieurs secrets et de rem?des pour les maladies et les playes.
mv5xn43z.c: Interspersed among the medical receipts are a number of veterinary entries of remedies for horses and cattle. The 28 ll. after the main text contain accounts for fees received by a Dijon lawyer from August 1781 to January 1791.

mv6hhshr.t: Croy, Anne de, Princesse de Chimay ( -1539).

The first 42 ff. ff are by the original hand: the remainder in different and somewhat later 16th cent. scripts: those on fol. lx are in Flemish.Signature of 'Damant' in a 16th cent. hand on the first leaf.

mvmzkpbc.t: A small extract of Avicenna's (Ibn Sina) Canon translated in Persian.

myfuqbsj.c: Collection of medical prescriptions [c. 1895], in a copy of 'Bell's Commonplace Book for the pocket' 1770, originally belonging to P. Fyers in 1787. The name of the original owner, P. Fyers, is found written inside the first fly-leaf, dated January 23, 1787. At the end of the 11 ll. he states that he has arrived at Madeira 20th of April 1787, and the last leaf is stamped 'P. Fyers. Edinburgh.' The medical receipts are presumably by W. Macmath and may perhaps be dated about 1895, though his signature under that of P. Fyers on the first fly-leaf is dated 12th April 1904. At the end of the volume there are seven figure drawings in pencil, perhaps also by him.

mykxff67.c: [Clavicules de] la vi humene rabit de [crossed through] Salomon traduittes du texte hebreux avec exatitude misse en fran?ois avec les figurre misterieusse pantoculle, talismans, cerclle caracterre et canderies. Title in coloured inks, some passages in the text in blue or red: illustrated by numerous pen-drawn figures of pentacles, sigils etc. in coloured inks, or plain black, a few unfinished. On the verso of the first leaf: 'Copi?s sur les originot de la biblioteque nationalle'. The spine is lettered: 'Clavicules de Rabbi Solomon. M.S.' and below 'St. Germain': this may be the celebrated adventurer calling himself the 'Comte de Saint Germain', who is said to have died in 1784, and was associated with Count Cagliostro.

mywcsvmx.c: Selecta ex eis quae D.O.M. abscondit a sapientibus, dispersit, deditque pauperibus ['praemissis constitutionibus' struck through] V.F.C. In French and Latin. Some leaves seem to have been taken out after p. 325, and the last 13 ll. are on the different paper. On p. 220 is a full-page pen-drawn illustration in red and black of alchemical apparatus, on pp. 108, 208, 240 smaller marginal drawings. On pp. 36, 45, 51, 68 small symbolic figures. Text within red rules, headings in red. On p. 128 'Anno Domini nostri J. C. 1687. Incoepi practicare opera praecedentia, cum labore magno ad finem perduxi'. On p. 132 'Opus ab amico perfectum 23a Aprilis 1701'. On the last leaf, by another hand, is the date 1782.

myzt5zgv.c: Dises Ertzney Biechl geherdt der edlen unnd T?gendthafften frauen Elisabet Schitzin 1581. A medical receipt book, with a farm account-book, etc. by various hands dated 1599-1626; containing also notes on wine making, etc. With later additions down to 1668. A foliation in pencil has been added. Ff. 2-19 Frau Schitzin's medical receipts. 20-210 Farm account books, etc. by various hands, dated 1599 (fol. 20) to 1668 (126v). 210v-221v Ein sch?n Weinbuch. By the earliest compiler. Fol. 225 Receipts for almond cakes, etc. By a later hand. There are a number of blank leaves [ff. 159-199] in the middle of the volume, and it has been largely scribbled over.

mzk7bc3k.c: Notebook of medical and culinary recipes compiled by Caleb Lowdham, or Loudham, and Jane Lowdham, his wife or daughter. With a few case histories. Most of the medical recipes are in the hand of Caleb Lowdham, who signed his name on the opening leaf. Underneath is the signature of Jane Lowdham, dated 1729, who seems to have contributed the cookery recipes. Some of the medical receipts and the case histories are in the hand of a son or daughter of Lowdham. The bulk of the recipes and case notes are struck through. f. 2r. 'In Broadhembery about a mile from the Town at a village called staverd lives Wm Somerys in his mead of 2 Acres called Broad mead grows an herb yt unlockt a Horse lock about the legg at least 10 times'. ff. 3v.-51r. miscellaneous medical, veterinary and culinary recipes. ff. 52r.-55r. two case histories, 1692-3. ff. 55r.-57r. medical recipes. ff. 58r.-59r. case of gangrene in a child at Topsham, 1696. f. 60r. 'to cure warts'. ff. 60v.-118r. blank. ff. 118v.-136v. medical and other recipes from published works. ff. 137r.-138r. blank. ff. 138v.-141v. partial list of contents.

mzq25yfu.c: Epitome of the 'Methodus medendi' books III VII. (Incomplete). Illuminated initial on Fol. 1 in gold and colours with marginal floreated decorations, containing a miniature, slightly rubbed, of a physician operating on the head of a seated patient and two assistants standing by. Written in double column of 39 lines to a column, in an Italian gothic book-hand. Other capitals and paragraph marks in alternate blue and red: headings in red.p.1, col. 1 (red) Incipit liber tercius de ingenio/sanitatis. ad laudem dei./[S]ICUT/OP/ER/AND/I SIG/NIFI/CATI/ONES/NERO Carissime Ab essentia nature/morbi conuenit considerari..p.104, col. 2 [Capitulum xv, Libri VII.] In cucurbitis forciata apua absinthii./From leaf 33 to the end, the leaves are palimpsest, and there are traces of an earlier script-possibly of the 13th cent. These include lists of office-holders in an unknown Italian city. On p.68 is a heading in red 'Ad of[f]icium Jurarie', and on p.77, also in red, 'Ad of[f]icium lignagii'.

n2cjbyd5.c: Collection of medical and cookery recipes, for the most part in a single hand of the later 17th century. Various authorities are named, including Dr Burgess (f. 3), Dr Bentley (f. 5), the Earl of Kildare (f. 9v.), the Baron of Kinderton (f. 12), Dr Brookes (f. 16v.), Dr Stephens (f. 26), Dr Needham (f. 29), Dr 'Willoby' (a recipe for 'the midwife pill', f. 43), Dr Knot (f. 55), Dr Griffiths (f. 65v.), and Dr Warren (f. 71). The principal compiler has penned an epigram on the first leaf: 'Spare not nor spend too much, bee this your care Spare but to spend, and onely spend to spare [text wanting] spends too much, may want and [text wanting] complaine [text wanting] spends best, that spares to spend againe'. Cf. MS.8575.

n2gmyakn.t: Anstey, Mary Ann & Fenwick, Diana Matilda.
n2gmyakn.c: Cookery-book, with some medical and household receipts.M.A. Anstey's entries end at p. 73; the remainder are by D. M. Fenwick, with additions by various hands, some pasted in.The latest date is 1828 (p. 439).

n4wbdxw2.t: Ostfrisisches rares Medicinbuch. Dasz man von den Kra?tern, Thieren, und Mineralien die H?lfsmittel genommen.
n4wbdxw2.c: Mainly in Low German, but with entries in Latin, French, Dutch, Italian and English. There is one receipt in English on pp. 170, 171 'A Made or artificiall Champene Wyne'. There are also some veterinary receipts, and others for varnishes, inks, etc. Pp. 285-end have a separate title 'Sonderbahre K?stliche Medicamenta', and seem to be by a slightly later hand.

n5gg96mv.c: A 17th century medical remedy book, all written in the same hand but with no date or author. There are several pages that have been torn out throughout the book, some of which are held at the end in a separate plastic wallet. However several names to come up that created a particular recipe include: Mrs Margery Hubert, Sir Richard Hubert, Dr Sanders, Sir Lionel Tallemack, Lady Bridgman and the initials LH.

n5nst8qw.c: Fragment of a volume of medical receipts: in German.

n7gkusag.c: Artzney Buchli mit villen bewahrten Mittlen. The entry on the recto of the last leaf is written in the compiler's 70th year, in a difficult script. His name is also found inside the upper cover, on which is also the date 1774. The MS. was compiled in his earlier years, and is clearly written.

n8crehbv.t: Fragment of an unknown medical work
n8crehbv.c: Fragment of an unknown medical work

n8dwpq96.c: Collection of 5 receipts, for heartache, lung disease, 'wenns' or tumours (2), and liver disease. Written by three different contemporary hands: in Anglo-Saxon. The first receipt is by Hand A, which is slightly angular; the second, fourth and fifth in a smaller script, Hand B: the third is more rounded, Hand C. The verso is blank, except for two lines of verse in a hand of s.xi, and, repeated, s.xii: 'Psallere qui docuit dulci modulamine sanctis / Nouerat iste deceem legis qui uerba dedisset'. These are the first two lines of a poem ascribed to St Jerome (M. Ihm, Epigrammata Damasi, 1895, no. 63).

n8j47q3y.c: Medical examination for life-insurance, 1898. Holograph extracts made by Dr. Buxton Shillitoe, with some added notes. Produced in London.

n9nrd77c.t: Collection of alchemical treatises, notes and extracts: in Latin and French (Miscellanea Alchemica X).
n9nrd77c.c: Collection of alchemical treatises, notes and extracts: in Latin and FrenchSome of the items are dated. No. 1. Tabula Smaragdina: 1588. 30 Sep. n85bv3nh.c: Collection of medical and household receipts and prescriptions by several hands: in English and Latin. The date 1826 occurs on p. 130 and 1831 on p. 93. Many of the receipts are in Latin: there are some veterinary receipts.

nabs6vbg.c: Collection of cookery, household and medical receipts. The receipts are written by several hands. On the recto of first leaf 'W. Lowther his book': this is probably Sir William Lowther of Marske [1670-1705]. There are also numerous entries bearing the names of other members of the family.Lower corner of first leaf torn off and repaired, damp-stains affecting the last 26 lines and causing loss of text.

nacu9mr9.c: Livre des drogues touchant la medecinne [sic] et l'appoticairerie ... 1710. Barbeyrac (C.). Trait? des maux v?n?riens. [Anon.] La mani?re de faire la pierre min?rale [with other medical receipts]. [Anon.] Exp?riences nouvelles de phisique et de m?decine. 1713. [Incomplete]. The first work starts on a page numbered 137, but pp. 1-136 do not seem to have formed part of this volume at any time. Contents: (1) Girard de Bergeries (J.). Livre des drogues (pp. 137-297); (2) Barbeyrac (C.). Trait? des maux v?n?riens (pp. 299-338); (3) [Anon.] La mani?re de faire la pierre min?rale [etc.] (pp. 341-372); (4) [Anon.] Exp?riences nouvelles [Incomplete] (70 pp.). Pasted on the upper cover is a label inscribed: 'Rem?des pour quelques maladies d'apr?s Mr. Girard': this is signed 'C. Meynard'.

nc8bbx72.c: ARZNEIBUCH worinn sicher Mittel f?r allerhand Krankheiten, und zugleich auch varia Secreta chymica befindlich. Nebst andere Kuriosit?ten mehr. In spite of the title as given above, the contents are almost entirely alchemical. Pp. 3-33 contain a long extract from the 'De lapide philosophorum' by Laurentius Ventura, which was first published at Basle in 1571: the remainder of the MS. consists of alchemical notes and receipts.

nctquwxk.c: Collection of ten full-page water-colour drawings, with MS. Latin descriptions in red, of alchemical apparatus, furnaces, etc. The date is found on the illustration of a mortar on the verso of the third leaf from the end.

nfe786e4.t: Bonifacius de Lupis, Founder's Will of the Hospital of Florence, extract.
nfe786e4.c: Contents1. ff. 1r-13r Bonfacius de Lupis, Founder's Will of the Hospital at Florence, extractTitle: 'Ordinamenta et instituta egregii militis domini Bonifacii de Lupis, Marchionis Soraniae pro eius hospitale de Florentia'Incipit: 'Cum ego Bonifacius de Lupis de Parma Soranie marchio huius hospitalis conditor...'Explicit: '...uel omni alio iure quo melius ualere poterint. et hoc per yesum christum dominum nostrum. Amen'.There are a few marginal annotations, in Latin and Italian, by various 15th cent. hands. The MS. is a copy of the relevant part of the Founder's Will relating to the Hospital at Florence, which was opened in 1387.

nfn83dce.t: A collection of recipes for medicinal waters and other remedies, in Latin and Langue d'Oc (Proven?al).
nfn83dce.c: A collection of recipes for medicinal waters and other remedies, in Latin and Langue d'Oc, on paper, France, mid 15th century. Contents1. f. 1r: Recipes for medicinal waters for fractures and wounds, in Latin.f. 1r: Incipit: Ad extrahendum ossa fracta a vulnere. Recype herbam que dicitur mater silve ...; Explicit: Ad sanandum vulnus ? et da de dicta aqua in potu.2. ff. 1v-10r: Recipes for medicinal waters from plants, in Latin, preceded by an index.The collection is similar to a French one entitled Eaux artificielles avec leurs vertus et propri?t?s, first printed at Vienne by Pierre Bouttellier (Schenck) about 1484 [ISTC ie00000200; GW 9165], and in several other 15th-century editions. There is also a section (ff. 240-245) in the French edition of the De proprietatibus rerum printed at Lyons by [Claude Davost], for Jean Genin le Dyamantier, in 1500 [1501?] [ISTC ib00149000; GW 3422], which seems to correspond with the present collection. f. 1v: Index: Sequitur Rubrica aquarum sequentium. / Primo aqua aurea ? Capilli veneris.f. 2r: Incipit: Sequntur [sic] plures aque et modus quomodo debent fieri. / Et primo aqua aurea sit hoc modo / Recype duas vel tres petras auri ...f. 10r, line

ngcxpnj6.t: Transcripts, extracts, and notes on alchemy: volume II.
ngcxpnj6.c: Transcripts, extracts, and notes on alchemy [etc.]. Vol. II. Partly holograph MSS. At the end of the third section are pen-drawings of tubes and a crucible; also a coloured drawing of a distilling apparatus. The first three items are holographs by Bacstrom.On the spine is a label inscribed 'MSS. on alchemy received from H[enry] C[owell] Boyes 1894.' This is a printed title to the collection, and is found on the spine of both volumes.

nm5z4mcf.c: The manuscript consists of one work and is a book of notes relating to the nature and medical properties of plants, animals, the winds, seasons, fruits, etc., mostly in respect of diet. The text-which is in the form of short entries of four or five lines-is written in black and red, by a neat humanistic hand. It was produced in Verona.Two pagination schemes are present which include an earlier pagination created by a sixteenth century hand-who also created the index-and a later foliation. The catalogue description is based on the foliation. ff. 1v-2r The work begins with a colophon f. 1v Mcccclxxiiii Codex Ludouici de Cendratis ciuis Veronensis: qui nullum aliud nouit imperium: nisi Serenissimum uenetorum Dominium cum turba natorum numero trigintaduorum ex unico Matrimonio?. f. 2r Opus naturae rerum compendiosum et eruditum: nec minus uarium quam ipsa natura.The name 'Cendratis' seems to have been written over another name which has been erased (see f. 1v). Above the line a later hand has written 'Prius fuerat mei Antonii de ...' The rest has been rubbed out.1. ff. 3r-102r Medical notesf. 3r Ficus Nature calide et humide in 1? ... f. 102r Auicule et turdi Nature c[alide] et sicce i

nmhpjchc.t: de Wignacourt, Alof (d. 1622), Grand Master of the Order of St John of Jerusalem.
nmhpjchc.c: A volume of notes and extracts relating to the life of Alof de Wignacourt. ff. 3r.-47r. 'Compendio della Vita ed Azzioni dell'Eminentissimo Signor Don Alofio de Wignacourt cinquantesimoterzo Gran Maestro della Sacra Militar Religione di San Giovanni Gerosolimitano'. This work was dedicated (f. 5r) to Wignacourt's nephew, Pierre Adrien de Wignacourt (d.1697), treasurer-general and later grand master of the Order of St John, by the author, Giovanni Antonio Bonvicini. The copyist has inserted (f. 4r.) an engraving of a bust of Alof de Wignacourt, aged sixty-one. ff. 47v.-49v. 'Ristretto delle pi? segnalate spese donativi ed imprestiti fatti dal Serenissimo Signore Gran Maestro Fra Alofio de Wignacourt in tempo del suo felicissimo magistero'. ff. 50r.-59v., 84r.-91r. Historical notes on the precedence of the flag of the Order of St. John. ff. 60r.-65v. 'Fra Alofio de Wignacourt, gia Ospedaliere, e Capo della Lingua di Francia 53o Gran Maestro, eletto nel 1601. nnkwd6zm.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few medical receipts. An added note on the first unnumbered leaf is dated 1809.

Darbey ist auch ein seer Kostlich und bewert Regiment der Pestilentz... The work is in four parts. 1. With title as above. (ff. 1-23.) 2. Ein ander Regiment zu Underhaltung menschlicher gesundheit dienstlich innsonderheit zur zeit der Pestilentz. (ff. 24-45.) 3. Ein kurtzer begriff wie eines yeden menschen harn zuerkennen, unnd was f?r kranckhaiten unnd gebrechlichait des Leibs daraus zu judicieren seind. (ff. 46-57.) 4. Allerlay gutte Recept inn Gemain f?r allerhand gebresten der menschen. (ff. 58-70.).

npev34ey.t: Ebrario, Un et altri buonissimi secreti.
npev34ey.c: Ricoreto da me et rinovato avendo levato moltisime sporchizie, dove si trova duetavol, una de secreti, e l'altra delli autori 1800. Questo e di Girolamo Genesini. There are 84 coloured and four uncoloured pictures of plants of medical use, in water-colour, mostly of a formal and crude design following the early printed Herbals. The original text seems to have been written by different hands, an entry by one of the later of these on fol. 111 being dated 1555. Another entry by one of the supplementary writers on fol. 106v is dated 1732, and some other additions seem even later. The indices were presumably the work of Genesini. The first and last plant illustrations have been pasted down, and are not included in the numbered foliation.

nqj699aj.t: This manuscript was al-Razi's work that pioneered the method of differential diagnosis now being used in the modern day medical field.
nqj699aj.c: This manuscript was al-Razi's work that pioneered the method of differential diagnosis now being used in the modern day medical field.

nr796xhj.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few household, medical, and veterinary receipts. The original compiler is Eliza Anna Smith whose name, with the date 1783 is found on p. 1: this section ends at p. 71. The remainder of the volume, with a few additions by later hands, one dated 1850 on p. 251, appears to be by the hand of Mrs. Loraine Smith whose name is inscribed outside the lower cover as 'Lauraine' (cf. pp. 183, 207).

Title: Item diss B?ch Ist Hanns Br?mmers / Von Rotwil und ist geschriben / worden Im Jar 1548. // [By a different hand] Urin dem schriber, dreck dem lesser // Von Ainer [?] Wolffgang Wippler // O wie fro ich was / Do ich schrib deo gratias. nuctgpjv.t: Libro intitulado de varios secretos de medesina [sic] y cirurjia, etc. Recopilados y esprimentados por mi ... cirurjano apraticant en la ciutat de Tarragona, etc. Frontispiece of a pen-drawing of SS.
nuctgpjv.c: Libro intitulado de varios secretos de medesina [sic] y cirurjia, etc. Recopilados y esprimentados por mi ... cirurjano apraticant en la ciutat de Tarragona, etc. Frontispiece of a pen-drawing of SS. Cosmas and Damian with an ornamented shield: large pen-drawn vignette of the B.V.M. supporting the dead Christ, with a similar shield. At the end a pen-drawing of the 'Vein Man'. There are additions by different hands. The date on the title-page has been altered. It seems to have been originally '1772', but the second seven has been written over so that it reads '1732'. On the penultimate leaf verso, is a remedy 'Contra la epilepsia' by a different hand, dated 1777. Some scribblings at the beginning and inside the volume, in which the name Francisco Piquer occurs several times. Produced in Tarragona.

nv4q76u5.c: Arvore da Vida dilatada em vistosos e salutiferos ramos ornados de muitas aprasiveis, e saudiveis folhas, em que se deixa? nver muitos e singulares remedios assim simplices, como compostos, que a Arte, e experiencia, a industria, e a curiosidade descubrio, para curarcom facilidade quasi todas as doen?as, e queixas, a que o corpo esta sogieto, principalmente em terras desitiduas de Medicos e Boticos. Copiados de diversos Authores assim impressos, como manuscriptos, de varias noticias e experiencias vistas e approvadas ... Offerecida ... pello Padre Affonso da Costa da Companha de Jesus dda Provincia de Goa. The first leaf contains a full-page historiated pen-drawing of the Tree of Life. At the end there is a very elaborate index. Produced at Goa, this MS. is a very carefully written scribal copy of a work prepared for publication, and dedicated to King John V of Portugal (1689-1750). No record of publication has been found: the author published a 'Methodo de bom viver: intinerario christia?' in 1716. Below the title, by another hand, 'Apilcado ao Cubiculo do P[adr]e R[ect]or do Nov[iciad]o.'

nvcg5ja5.t: Malauze, Guy Henri, de Bourbon, Marquis de (1654-1706).
nvcg5ja5.c: La grande Mareschalerie de Monseigneur le Marquis de Malauze. Contenant les dozes et compositions qui apportent de grands soulagemens aux chevaux, avec l'argument ou Ethimologie de grand Mareschal et Anathomie du Cheval. A very well-written copy, probably by a professional scribe. The attribution to this Marquis de Malauze is conjectural, and no record of this work has been traced.

nvfuxu2k.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few medical receipts: by several hands.

nvm2r66t.c: Receipt book containing medical and cookery receipts: with numerous later additions by various hands, including some household and miscellaneous receipts. The original entries, perhaps written c. 1750, are in a large italic script and are scattered throughout the volume between p. 11 and p. 288. The largest group seems to have been written in the first quarter of the 19th cent., and many of the receipts are dated: the latest date is 1853 on p. 302. Pp. 96-99 contain prescriptions, etc. for Fr. Smyth Esqre. and Mrs. Smyth by Alexander Hunter [1729-1809] dated 1788, and by Thomas Kilvington [1732-1823], dated 1795 and 1797.

nxjfykmd.t: Sophia Jex-Blake: copy book of letters and other documents.
nxjfykmd.c: Copy book kept by Sophia Jex-Blake with copies of her letters, reviews and other writings for the years c.1883-1888. It has been written in starting at both ends. It includes drafts of her work on on the care of infants (published in 1884), ff 1-192v; "Things that Women Ought to Know ", ff 193-253; notes on and review of Theodore Stanton The Woman Question in Europe (ff. ff 495v-471v ). There are drafts or copies of letters to editors of assorted periodicals on a variety of subjects, medical and non-medical, including "Medical Education for Women", "Maternity Hospitals" and "First Places for Young Girls"; materials relating to medical education for women, especially the Edinburgh Medical School or Women, and to the Hospital for Women and Children. A number of matters of personal administration, some of them dealt with by Margaret Todd, are also contained in this volume.

nxmgy548.c: A dictionary of simple and compound medicines with alphabetical arrangement. Each entry includes: a vocalization of the name of the medicine, its physical description (e.g. colour and texture) as well as remarks on its origin (Indian, Persian, Greek etc.). Some entries also have a brief description of the properties of the medicine.

nxp89hrx.c: Collection of medical receipts in Italian and Latin. (Incomplete.) Fol. 88 is doubled in the original foliation. The headings seem to have been added by a different, and somewhat later hand.

nxuzesvh.c: Collection of medical receipts and prescriptions: in German and Latin. The text is written by the same hand throughout.

This would be Carolus Battus the translator of G?belkhover's 'Booke of Physicke', printed at Dort in 1599. 'Old Dr Jonathan Wood's Receipts. Cost 6s beside Entertainment September 10. 1707' (fol. 9). 'Out of the "Nature of things" by Paracelsus' (fol. 13). There are several extracts and receipts from 'The English Physician' and other works by Nicholas Culpeper [1615-1654]. pg4yybx3.t: Johannes de Rupescissa, De consideratione quintae essentiae.
pg4yybx3.c: Johannes de Rupescissa, De consideratione quintae essentiae, in Latin, on paper, Northern Italy (Bologna or Padua?), late 15th century.Contents1. ff. 1-22v, 22v-30v: Johannes de Rupescissa (Jean de Roquetaillade), De consideratione quintae essentiae, in Latin.The treatise, probably written by Rupescissa about 1351-1352, describes the alchemical processes for the extraction by distillation of the essence of wine, plants and minerals for medicinal purposes. The distillation of the aqua ardens (ethyl alcohol) extracted from wine is at the basis of all other distillations. The author believes the alcohol to be an element similar to the so-called quinta essentia, the incorruptible fifth element that according to Aristotle forms the essence of heavenly bodies, and is therefore capable of preserving the human body from corruption and illnesses. The text is divided into two books, the first dedicated to the distillation processes with subdivisions called canones, the second to the medical applications of the essences described, arranged in chapters called remedia.The text is listed in eTK, A digital resource based on Lynn Thorndike and Pearl Kibre, A Catalogue of Incipits of Medieval Scien

pgynnb7e.c: RECEPTES aux maladies. A collection of medical, cosmetic, veterinary, cookery, and other receipts, by several hands: in French. There are two early foliations, one in Roman, the other in Arabic figures, both of which seem to be irregular: and one section iiiixx-C21 is misbound at the end. A new foliation in pencil has been made from which it appears that leaves are wanting after ff. 78, 121, 133, 135, 154, 161, 164. Ff. 3, 4 contain an index to the leaves originally foliated in Roman numerals. In the upper margin of the first leaf is a faded inscription 'Bibliotte[ca] [?] Sancti Andreae in Nemure [sic]. Fol. 7 contains a rough circular pen-drawing of the Elements, etc. Ff. 7v, 8 contain number tables, the latter dated 1548. In the lower margin of fol. 9 the name 'Blendecque' in a 16th cent. hand. On fol. 139: 'Monsieur Monsieur Le R?u?rend Pr?lat de l'abbaye de St. Andr? au Bois [?] pr?sentemen[t] r?fugi? ? Hesdin. Audict lieu.' by a middle 16th cent. hand.

phvt5ez9.c: Collection of medical receipts, with a few cookery receipts: in English. The name of Anne Nevile is found on the verso of the last leaf, and she may have been the compiler of this MS. Signature of 'William Clarke, Ashby 1810' inscribed inside the upper cover.

pjkq6d75.c: The extract or tables of Rotalo, 1500...The hidden Treasure. Look for a algebraical number to sport at the Lottery, at Room, established with all perfection upon mathematical, astronomical and algebraical points planely denoted, not without much study and application by T. M. N. 1744. Inserted are five pen-drawn diagrams of fortune-telling wheels, three possibly contemporary with the MS, one dated 1855, in red and black, and a Tibetan block-print. On the verso of the penultimate leaf of the MS. is a note of 'Numbers calculated by Count Cagliostro for the Lottery 1776 in London'. The water-mark on the paper is dated 1794. An extract from an undated sale catalogue of Sotheby's, states that 'The original of this book was in the Vatican Library, and was death for any person to copy, but was written out from memory by a monk who visited it daily till he had effected his purpose. Dr. Sibly gave 300 guineas for permission to copy it. From this work Cagliostro learnt his surprising feats'. The date 1500 is obviously incorrect, as Ansaloni was born in 1523 and died in 1599, but it seems very probable that 'Rotalo' is a scribal mis-reading for 'Rutilio'.

pjzv8cqp.c: A beautifully written uncial Latin manuscript, by the same scribe throughout with elaborate capitals in red and blue. The initial capital letter of each book is very large and elaborate, using gold and floral designs. The contents are as follows:- The Passionarius of Gariopontus, one of the early teachers of the School of Salerno (died 1050). The work is a manual of special pathology and therapeutics of Byzantine origin, translated and edited by by Gariopontus. The work was formerly, but erroneously, attributed to Galen. Gariopontus is the earliest writer to mention an?sthesia by inhalation of narcotic vapours. The treatise is divided as follows: Prolegomena (fo. 1r); Book i, On diseases of the head, brain and nerves, 21 chapters (fo. 2r-19r); Book ii, Diseases of the lungs and thoracic viscera, 38 chapters (fo. 19v-46r); Book iii, Diseases of the abdominal and pelvic viscera, 60 chapters (fo. 46r-79v); Book iv, Diseases of the muscles and articulations, 24 chapters (fo. 79v-89r); Book v, Diseases of the skin and other eruptive diseases, 31 chapters (fo. 89r-127v); Book vi, On Fevers, 44 chapters (fo. 127v-158r); Book vii, On Fevers (continued), 20 chapters (fo. 158r-173v).

pkcehw53.c: Recueil de rem?des. Author's holograph MS. Many of the entries are for cures of venereal diseases, and include on p. 94bis, p. 94ter, 'Traitement anti-v?n?rien que l'on emploit ? l'H?pital Militaire (V?n?rien) de Toulouse 1841'. Pp. 329-340 contain 'Collection de vernis d'apr?s Tingry et Watier'. Pierre Fran?ois Tingry [1743-1821] was a Swiss chemist whose work on varnish was published in 1803. Watier has not been identified. There are also other entries in varnishes, dyes and colours. Pp. 345-427 contain 277 numbered receipts headed 'Collection de rem?des tir?s de la M?decine primitive' i.e. from 'Primitive medicine' by John Wesley [1703-1791], first published in 1747: there was a French translation, which appeared in 1772. These receipts have a separate index. Pp. 445-454 'Diverses recettes tir?es d'un livre espagnol imprim? ? Logro?o 1843'. This has not been identified, and the collection is unfinished. The first leaf is inscribed 'Manuscrit Lacaze P?re. Vol. 4'. Produced in Toulouse.

pm9pa96s.t: Recueil de rem?des et de recettes. By several hands.
pm9pa96s.c: This collection contains many cookery receipts, especially for sirops and drinks, also veterinary and household receipts. It seems to have been begun perhaps c. 1785, and the later entries are probably of the early 19th cent.

pmby6puy.c: Planetarium: opus de fabrica horarii magistralis. Written in a semi-currenthumanistic hand, 30 lines to a page. Some initials and headings in red, much faded. Illustrated with 59 pen-drawings of parts of the clock, etc.: of these, 33 are coloured. There are also many smaller illustrations of minior pieces of mechanism. The colourings are in water-colour and gold paint. Inside the lower cover is a 17th cent. pen and ink drawing, showing three men standing outside the door of a house, one bare-headed, holding a jug [?]. Fol. 1 (Text begins) et calculationis tedio ac si ad dictam horam fuerit cum tabulis operatus modicissima/et paruae curae si qua interueneit differentia uarietatis... 14, line 1 ...Fuit namque/huius temporis. scilicet. 1364. anno christi perfecto secundum tabulas alfonsi in fine ge/-minorum... 83v ... Et sic/eo situato reduc deorsum ut denticuli inzegnonsis reinserantur cum/sua rotula et in axicula reimpone cauillam sicque dimitte.//Factus est hic liber Anno Domini 1364. ut colligitur/ex principio pagine 14.

pmgj9aex.c: Collection of cookery, medical and household receipts. Written by an early 19th cent. hand, except for the last 5 ll., which include a receipt for 'mushroom catchup', taken from 'Apicius redivivus' by William Kitchener [1775-1827]: this was first published in 1818, and there were several later editions, the seventh in 1827.

pn3nux9s.c: Liber luminum minus et perfecti magisterii. Abridged and incomplete. Written in a small cursive gothic hand 46 lines to a page: capitals in red and black, paragrpah marks in black. Fol. 1 [Q]uoniam solem [sic for 'solertis'] indagine vniuersarum rerum artificia philosophia com/perit sedulitate... 12v [...morari in eo trib]us diebus sed omni die contere vitriolum/The verso of the last leaf is almost entirely illegible, but the end of the last line appears to read as above. This would correspond to the middle of the receipt for Oleum rubicundum fixum philosoplucum' on p. 113 of Vol. III of Zetzner's 'Theatrum Chemicum', 1659, who assigns this work to Aristotle. This would seem incorrect, and the Tract is rightly attributed to Rhazes, as in Singer's Catalogue of Alchemical MSS., No. 114.

pnv8kxa7.c: RECEIPT-BOOKS, Latin: Before 1500. Collection of medical receipts by an anonymous Italian physician: in Latin. Written in a rounded Italian cursive hand 29-30 lines to a page. The text contains mainly medical receipts, but there are a few chemical, household and technical receipts. There is a long section (ff. 12v-19v) 'Ad diversas passiones oculorum', and a number of receipts for toothache, etc. Included are several incantations and magical remedies some of which have been crossed through. The water-mark most frequently found seems to be Briquer No. 786 (Lucca. 1372).

ppew92xx.t: 1 copy of Jumlat khawāṣṣ mufīdah by an anonymous author
ppew92xx.c: 1 copy of Jumlat khawāṣṣ mufīdah by an anonymous author

pprrvkyt.c: Palaeographia sacra or Discourses on monuments of Antiquity that relate to sacred history. Number II. A dissertation on the Mysterys of the Antients, being an explanation of the Table of Isis, or Bembine Table. Author's holograph MS. Illustrated by inserted engraved plates, including the complete 'Table of Isis' (folding) and parts of it cut out as separate plates. On fol. 16 is an original pencil drawing of Horus by the author; it has not been completed. Pasted in the lower cover is a drawing of 'The geometry of the Duke of Mountagu's bridg 17 Sep. 1744', also by the author. On verso of the title, armorial book-plate of the St. John Family. MS. 4722 is an earlier draft of this work, dated 1735-40. Produced in Stamford.

pptxfwdg.t: Journal while assistant surgeon on board HMS Cleopatra, on anti-slavery patrols off the coast of East Africa.
pptxfwdg.c: On anti-slavery patrols off the coast of East Africa, especially Madagascar, Mozambique and Zanzibar. The journal includes information on health conditions and medical provision on board ship, and amongst the Portuguese settlers and the native population on the coast.

ppzy6cf8.t: Giordano Ruffo, Le medicine de' cavalli: diseases and remedies only.

Titles in Latin, with main text in ItalianIncipit: 'In hoc uolumine continentur diuerse infir/mitates accidentales Equorum vnde proueniant et remedia opportuna. Et primo de verme. pqra6nkd.c: Collection of cookery receipts, by several hands.

pr5t8z6k.c: Material formerly held in the Western Manuscripts Department's Autograph Letters Sequence.

prcyjse5.c: Ein gutt Khunst undt Artzney Buch von allerley Khranckheiten undt Schmertzen...Ausswendig undt Ihnwendlig dess Leibs...von wiederschiedliche Hern Doctor [sic] geschrieben... As the original pagination is irregular, a new foliation in pencil has been added. The first leaf and some headings, etc. written in red ink. Ff. 86-119 contain receipts by a different and later 17th cent. hand, and include some incantations. There are also some charms among the receipts on ff. 119v-129 written in an early 18th cent. script. Produced in Amberg.

prrf9sds.c: Collection of cookery and medical receipts. Inserted is an 8vo. sheet (paper) containing a priced list of food and drink, probably for a village feast. Among the items are: 6 swans for 15/-, II gallons of red wine for 9/2, and 200 eggs for I/6. This is written by the same hand as that of the MS. itself. The upper cover is lettered 'Herbes to season, herbes to cure'. Inside the upper cover in red ink 'Grace Acton, May 1621'.Research by social historian of food culture Ivan Day suggests that MS.1 is not a genuine receipt collection but a fake constructed sometime in the 19th- or early 20th-century using elements from a 17th-century notebook.The handwriting appears to be a pastiche script rather than a genuine hand of the period, and while the medicinal recipe ingredients largely reflect genuine pre-modern remedy ingredients, they are all somewhat outlandish, suggesting that the author has either selected genuine recipes for bizarre effect, or has conflated unusual ingredients into fake remedies. Notably, however, the cough remedy on p.4 contains the anachronistic ingredient glycerine, a chemical compound not discovered until 1779 by the Swedish chemist Carl Wilhelm Scheele.As regards

ps6jcsqm.t: A composite medical manuscript of three separate works.
ps6jcsqm.c: A composite medical manuscript of three separate works.

pstu5q9d.c: Collection of medical, veterinary and household recipes in a single hand, late 18th-early 19th century (paper watermarked 1794). Various authorities are named, including Lady E Hatton (ff.6, 15, 55v.), Dr Wilmot (ff. 18, 56), Dr Kelson (f. 20v), Dr Thornton (f. 25), Dr Whitton or Whitter (ff. 27v., 53), Sir William Knighton [1776-1836, physician to the Prince Regent] (f. 31v.), Dr Babbington [presumably William Babington MD, 1756-1833] (f. 32v.), Lady Heron (f. 45v.), Dr Birdwood (f. 48v.), and Dr Mayo (f. 59). There is also a prescription for cholera dated July 1832, from Mr Earle, surgeon (f. 63v.), and a remedy for ̀the epidemic amongst cattle 1840' (f. 69v.).

pt5h2vvx.c: Collection of medical, cookery, and household receipts: with additions by several hands. With numerous inserted receipts and cuttings from newspapers, etc. pasted in. An inscription inside the upper cover, partly struck through, reads: 'This Recipe Book was begun by Mrs. Finger [?] who died in 1770. And I began going on with it March 20th A.D. 1779. Anna Maria Reeve, Hendens, Berks'. The collection therefore may have been begun c. 1750. The latest dated receipt is 1800.

pvtnggrg.c: Written in a small gothic hand, in double column of 53-55 lines to a column, between red and black rules in the design of Norman arches with two large and one small light at the top for the first work; and without the top light in the second work. The top light contains a few lines of text belonging to the first column. Initials in alternate blue and red, headings in red. Illustrated on f. 4r with a diagram of five interlocking circles in red, green and black, containing Roman letters and numerals; and on f. 7v with the Spheres of Pythagoras' in red and black.Contents1. ff. 1r-7v Alchandrus, De naturis planetarum, beginning wanting and preceded by a fragment of a text on the planetsThe Alchandreana texts were the first Arabic astrological treatises to be translated into Latin in the tenth century. See David Juste, Les Alchandreana primitifs: ?tude sur les plus anciens trait?s astrologiques latins d'origine arabe (Xe si?cle) (Leiden: Brill, 2007).(begins imperfectly) '...ipsa erit quasi humida?[first complete entry f. 1r col. 1] Saturnus in quo signo....De naturis planetarum. Luna nature frigide coloris argentei...'Explicit: '?ambiguo erit.'2. f. 7v Two redactions of the 'Sphere of

pwgaeypq.t: Jacopo Florentino, Fiore de fiori, with medical receipts.

Allo honore et a la reverentia de la sanctissima trinitade la quale ordino tutto quello che se vede et che non se vede in celo et in terra ... f. 1v Voglio che sapiati che nui aporemo le cure de tutto il corpo. In co mmenciando dai capilli e seguitando per ordine a ciaschuno membro in fino a li piedi. etc. ... f. 62v ... metti vno pocho di sarcorrella et eprovato. finis libri etc.2. ff. 63r-64r Medical receipts in Italian3. ff. 64r-71r Domenico Bandini, Receptariaf. 64r Oleum magistri bandini medici florentini quod pro maximo habebat secreto alias balsamus artificialis vocatum ... f. 71r finis receptorium magistri bandini medici florentini quod pro maximo habebat secreto. laus deo omni potenti etc.4. ff. 71r-80r Medical receipts in Latin and Italian5. ff. 80v-84v, Carlo da Cantiano, Receptae, in Italianf. 80v Ceroto de mastro carlo da chantiano. Galbano 1 ... f. 84v ... pezze de lino vechie et operate alli sangnio.

pwn4wxzs.c: Written in a neat humanistic hand, 18 lines to page. Illuminated initial R on first leaf in gold and colours, with marginal decoration: other initials in alternate brown and blue, headings in red: the Index is wholly written in red. Fol. 1 (red) Tractatus De uenenis a magistro Pe/tro de Abbano editus.//[R]Euerendissimo in chri/sto patri et domino. N.//diunia prouidentia summo/pontifici... 50, line 16 ... et ideo mater/omnium medicinarum a medicis est/appellata. 50v (red) Tabula capitulorum.//De prologo 1. 53 Questio utrum tiriaca etc. 83. The pagination has been cut out in binding. Below the text on fol. 1 are the emblazoned arms, within a gold circle and wreath, of an unidentified cardinal. The last leaf is blank except for four lines of Latin verse, written in an 18th century. hand.

pwwqcv8q.t: Kunst-Buch enthaltned allerley Mittel und Kunste f?r Menschen, Pferde, Fische und Krebse.
pwwqcv8q.c: Written by the same hand throughout. There are a few later additions by other hands, including a few by Georg Stekermayr whose signature is on the recto of the first leaf. The title given above is that written on the verso of the first leaf by another anonymous owner and dated 17/6/1845. Contents: pp. 1-70. Miscellaneous medical, technical, household and cookery receipts. 71-101. Allerhandt andere Kunst und Merckwurdigkeiten. 103-121. Von der G?rtnerey und allerhandt Kraitlwerckh. 123-128. Vom Fischen. 129-138. Golt und Silber zu machen. Register (2 unnumbered ll.). 139-202. Neuzugericht und vermehrt wie auch in villen verbesserte und mehrsten theils approbirte Ross-Arzney. 203 Character oder Zeichen des Apotheker-Gewichts. Register ?ber dass Ross-Arzney Buchlein (2 ll.). At the end are some receipts by several late 18th cent. or early 19th cent. hands, and the address in Augsburg of a Philipp Jacob Sch?r, who made a special balsam.

pxpebuwk.t: Prayers of magical character, with 3 coloured magical pictures.
pxpebuwk.c: Prayers of magical character, with 3 coloured magical pictures.

pz6y72ru.c: Her receipt Book. A collection of cookery and medical receipts. On the third leaf before the end of the cookery receipts 'Finished by Mrs. George Rye June 14th, 1787. Darling Hall'. The medical receipts begin at the other end of the volume, on the first leaf of which is inscribed: 'Mrs. George Rye May 29th 1786' and below 'Catherine Rye her receipt Book dated in the year 1786'. 'Domina Rye ejus liber' beneath this seems to be by a different hand.

q2cm3a7u.c: R?flexions sur le magn?tisme [animal]. Author's holograph MS. On the fly-leaf is written 'Ce manuscrit est de la main de M. Gombaut, ancien magistrat et ami de M. de St. Martin', signed 'S[imon] Mialle'.

q2uu22c6.c: Notes of lectures at the Universities of Franeker and Nijmegen on the Institutes of Medicine, and on Cartesian Philosophy: in Latin. Holograph MS. by de Mandeville, written while a medical student. Contents: [Anon.]. Philosophiae moralis epitome (9 ll.). Matthaeus (Philippus) [1621-1700] In alma Frisiorum (quae est Franequera) Universitate observations in ... D. Alberti Kyperi Institutiones medicas (88 pp.). Radiis (Johannes de) Dictata ad Epitomen Institutionum medicarum Danielis Sennerti. 1656 (129 pp. + 29 ll.). Pp. 113-125 contain 'D. Johannis Antonidae van der Linden [1609-1664] Doctrina de febribus'. Wittich (Christophorous [1623-1687] In alma Gelriorum (quae est Noviomagi) Universitate, Observationes in Renati Descartes Meditationes de prima philosophia (35 ll.). Observations in ejusdem Principiorum philosophiae partem primam [only] (4 ll.). Inside the cover is the date 1656, and three signatures of de Mandeville, with one in Greek, and another dated 1664. Below, signature of John Lee [1783-1866], antiquarian and scientist 'J. Lee Doctors Commons No. 390. Recovered Mr Wilson, London'. Produced in Franeker & Nijmegen.

q4de9uxq.t: Single leaf from a folding almanac, second half of the fifteenth century, including calendar information and medical summaries.
q4de9uxq.c: Calendarium. Containing Festa mobilia, Tabula planetarum, Homo venarum, Tabula lunae. Written in red and black in a neat gothic script. Initials in alternate red and blue for the Vein section and the Moon tables. There is a rough outline pendrawing in red of a male figure to illustrate the 'Homo venarum'. Title in alternate red and black: 'Indictiones/ffesta mobilia/Tabula planetarum/Homo venarum/Tabula lune'.

q5d83734.d: Mid 15th century, the first text dated 1430
q5d83734.c: Collection of three alchemical works by Jean Saulnier, Johannes de Rupescissa and Arnoldus de Villanova, with the addition of some alchemical receipts. The first work is in French, the remainder in Latin. q5jt2ejp.c: 18th century culinary and medical recipe book.Unindexed.The volume comprises mainly culinary recipes and is written in two hands.ff. 1-2. blankff. 3-42. Mainly culinary recipes, including sections for puddings, cakes, and wines. Most of the recipes are attributed to one of the following: Lady Ka Paule, Mrs Swain, Mrs Clitheron, or Mrs Hyde. q8vragr7.c: CABALE Sacr?e et Divine Des Soixante et Douze Noms des Anges qui portent le Nom de Dieu, qui furent r?v?l?s par le Saint Ange Metatron ? n?tre Pere Mo?se par moyen desquels on obtiendra Des Anges, comme lui, tout ce qu'on leur demandera de licite et permis, lors qu'on sera en ?tet [sic] de Gr?ce. q28racs8.c: Commentary on the Hippocratic Aphorisms by Ḥunayn b. Isḥāq

q45fgz49.t: Gerardus Bituricensis, Glossae super Viatico [Constantini Africani].
q45fgz49.c: Glossae super Viatico [Constantini Africani]. In this MS., wrongly ascribed to Gerardus Cremonensis. Written in double column of 56 lines to a column in a small gothic script. Ornamental initial in red and blue with marginal decoration on fol. 1, other initials in red, headings in red. Fol. 1 (red) Incipiunt Glosule magistri Gerardi cremonensis super viatico. capitulum. 1. de allopicia. col. 1 Cum omnia ex 4 elementis generata a medicis quodam modo sint/cognoscenda... 56v, col. 2 ... betonice/radix quedam est que in india habundat et inde nobis affertur/similis est radice rubee maioris. calida. et sicca... This passage is found on fol. 190v, col. 2, lines 11, 12 in the printed edition of Venice 1505 of the 'Opera' of Gerardus de Solo, who should be more properly called Gerardus Bituricensis. Some marginal notes by contemporary and 15th cent. hand.

q94kzuq7.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few medical receipts: by various hands. The date 1781 is found on p. 62, but many entries seem to belong to the first quarter of the 19th cent.

q64854un.c: Account book of a retail chemist. Partly compiler's holograph MS. The compiler had a chemist's business in Thorne near Doncaster, and the entries until 1892 are holograph: later entries are by several different hands. The last 34 ll. starting from the other end of the volume contain a holograph Day Book for 1847-1852, from which it appears that Armitage was also a grocer, and kept a general store: he also sold 'British Wines'.

qabd6bqc.t: Arabic letter written from Aḥmad (?) to Muḥammad Afandī Ibrāhīm
qabd6bqc.c: Arabic letter written from Aḥmad (?) to Muḥammad Afandī Ibrāhīm

qajajvzr.c: Collection of medical receipts, mainly in Italian, but a few in Latin: preceded by some short sermons on Biblical texts. By several hands. The sermons occupy the first 62 leaves, there is further theological matter on ll. 7-75, and ll. 114-124, including the ceremonies for Blessing of Water. On ll. 80v and 81 are special prayers against snake-bite, poison and the plague. On l. 76 two rough pen-drawings of a ligature to be worn to stop bleeding at the nose. On ff. 67, 69v is an Italian poem on Alexander the Great, and on fol. 69 some Latin verses. The date 1545 is found on l. 63 and l. 77. The entries are by several contemporary hands.

qakb273h.c: 1 text on astronomy in Persian and 1 text on grammar in Arabic

qap7puqr.t: A manuscript about various medicines relating to the heart, written by Ibn Sina for a nobleman.
qap7puqr.c: A manuscript about various medicines relating to the heart, written by Ibn Sina for a nobleman.

qav844sz.c: Liber de formulis remediorum ex Galenicis et Chimicis. (Followed by) De signis morborum; and medical receipts in Latin, with a few in French. Inside upper cover 'ad usum J. Garnier. d.M. anno 1767': and on a leaf pasted on the lower cover, '1767 ad usum Joannis Garnier scriptus hic liber'.

qay8y64b.c: Aphorismi (incomplete). Written in a neat upright gothic book-hand. Large initial in blue at the beginning of each 'Particula', other capitals in red, or tinted in yellow. (Begins) (red) PRIMA PARTICVLA AFFORISMORVM.///[V]ITa breuis. Ars vero longa. Tempus acutum experimentum/fallax... (End) Ex inflammatione epatis singultus malum. The last Aphorism is No. XVII of Section VII in Haller's 'Artis medicae principles', p. 492. (Edit Lausanne, 1787. Vol. I.).

qd2kk3q8.c: Collection of medical and cookery receipts: with additions by several hands: in English. Ff. 7-38 are headed 'Phisikale Resepts for all Deseses': many of the entries are by very illiterate hands. On the verso of the last leaf are notes of books, the latest dated 1718. An inscription 'William White his boock' on the first leaf has been struck through.

qduqfunf.c: Mrs Anne Brumwich her Booke of Receipts or Medicines ffor severall sores and other Infermities. With many additions, by several later 17th cent. hands. The original compiler, Anne Brumwich, writes in an early 17th cent. hand, but some of the additions are much later, one dated 1681 is found on p. 12.

qe7kbwa7.c: Anatomia del corpo umano. Cavata dalla prosa, ristretta, e spiegata in ottava rima. The poem on 'Anatomia' is complete: and is followed by three sonnets. At the end of the 'Anatomia' is a colophon: 'Terminando con universale applauso / Il Signore Candido del Negro La / Camerario del pio luogo, ed assumendola / Il Signore Ognibene Vatallo'. The latter appears to be the author of the sonnets.

qed7ztf4.c: Commonplace book containing notes on veterinary medicine, racing and race horses, tropical hygiene, household receipts; and extracts on historical and poetical subjects. Writer's signature inside cover. The main entries seem to have been made in 1823, the last date of the winners of the Doncaster St. Leger Stakes: but at the end there is an entry dated 1826.

qehycywh.t: විමාන වත්ථුප්පකරණය ත්‍රිපිටකයේ ඛුද්දක නිකායට අයත් ග්‍රන්ථකි. කරන ලද කුසලාකුසල විපාක වශයෙන් නැවත උත්පත්තිය ලැබූ තැන්වල විස්තර විමානවත්ථුවේ දැක්වෙයි. කුසල අකුසල හා එහි විපාක පැහැදිලි කිරීමට විමානවත්ථුවෙ
qehycywh.c: විමාන වත්ථුප්පකරණය ත්‍රිපිටකයේ ඛුද්දක නිකායට අයත් ග්‍රන්ථකි. කරන ලද කුසලාකුසල විපාක වශයෙන් නැවත උත්පත්තිය ලැබූ තැන්වල විස්තර විමානවත්ථුවේ දැක්වෙයි. කුසල අකුසල හා එහි විපාක පැහැදිලි කිරීමට විමානවත්ථුවෙයි එන විස්තර භාවිත වී ඇත. මෙම ග්‍රන්ථය විමාන වත්ථුවෙහි සත්වන වග්ගය පාලි භාෂාව නොදන්නවුන් සඳහා සිංහල බසින් කරල ලද විවරණයක් සේ ලියා ඇත. ශ්‍රී පුෂ්පාරාමයෙහි (වර්තමාන මල්වතු මහාවිහාරය) වැඩ වසමින් කීර්ති ශ්‍රී රාජසිංහ රජතුමන් විසින් දෙන ලද ප්‍රත්‍ය පරිභෝග කරමින්, ගලගෙදර ඉන්ද්‍රජෝති නම් හිමියන්ගේ ආරාධනයෙන්, රතනපාල ස්ථවිරයන් වහන්සේ විසින් මෙම ග්‍රන්ථය සම්පාදනය කරවා ඇත. එහි අවසනට ශාසන වත නමින් තවත් ග්‍රන්ථයක් සම්පාදනය කරමින් සැදැහැතියන් විසින් පැවැතිය යුතු ආකාරය දක්වමින් කරුණු සංග්‍රහ කර ඇත. එහි දැක්වෙන බොහෝ තොරතුරු ඓතිහාසික වශයෙන් ඉතා වැදගත් කමක් උසුලයි. මල්වතු මහා විහාරය මූලික කරගෙන ත්‍රිපිටක අට්ඨකථා සහිත විනය පිටකය දිවා රාත්‍රී හැදෑරීමක් පිළිබඳවව ද, සංඝරාජයන් වහන්සේ මුල්කරගනිමින් සිදු වූ ශාසන ශෝධනය ද ආදී ඉතා වැදගත් බොහෝ ශාසනික තොරතුරු මෙහි ඇතුළත්ව ඇත.
