qephb2j5.c: Volume 3 (covering 1657-1675). Comprises microfilm copies of the original minute book pages, which have been printed and bound together. Wellcome does not hold the original minute book.

qfrqk6mc.c: Collection of pharmaceutical receipts and prescriptions in systematic order: with a 'Trattato di chimica' on mineral materia medica, and a large selection of prescriptions, etc. extracted mainly from 17th and early 18th cent. authors. In Italian and Latin. Contents: Index and collection of preparations from animal substances (18 ll.). Prescriptions and preparations from vegetable materia medica, divided into 34 sections, pills, unguents, oils, powders etc. (ff. 1-187). Trattato di chimica [farmaceutica], and a collection of chemical and mineral prescriptions and remedies (ff. 187v-233). Trattato de' preparationi necessarie ad ogni Spetiale (ff. 234-240). Trattato di diversi remedi, d'alcuni chiamati Secreti (ff. 241-303). Schroeder (J.) 'Characteres': from his Pharmacopoeia medico-chymica (fol. 304). Further notes on animal materia medica (ff. 305-307). The date 1740 appears on fol. 266.

qftazqnx.t: Bonaventura da Iseo, Liber Compostelle, with additional alchemical recipes in Italian and Latin.
qftazqnx.c: An alchemical compilation in Latin and Italian copied in Italy in the early 15th century and including the Liber Compostella attributed to Bonaventura da Iseo.Contents:1) ff. 1r-1v Alchemical recipes in Latin and Italian vernacular (the first incomplete), reading: 'pone in furnum defensori et convertetur in aquam ?', 'Recipe salnitrum [oncie] vi suricara [oncie] vi ?', 'Ad solem / Recipe tutia [corrected into tutiba?] [once] I de rame purgata [once] i de sterco de surici ?', late 14th or 15th century.2) ff. 2r-107v, line 7, Bonaventura da Iseo (or Bonaventura da Brescia/da Ivreo; before 1200-c. 1260/1273), Liber Compostella [Compostelle, Compostille], imperfect: wanting the initial prologue to the whole work, prologues to Book 1 and 2, a few chapters in Book 2, and most of Book 3 with the exception of the prologue and a few initial recipes.The Liber Compostelle or Compostella is traditionally attributed to Bonaventura da Iseo, an influential Italian Franciscan and a well-known author of religious sermons in Latin. This traditional attribution, however, is possibly spurious and still a debated question.The compilation is a theoretical and practical guide to alchemy, which draws from

qfyv55yd.c: Collection of cookery receipts, and a few medical receipts: with additions by various hands. Inside the upper cover is an inscription: 'Sar[ah] Nott her Book given me by my Dear Spouse in the year 1701'.

qgbggavv.c: Collection of menus, with diagrams of the lay-out of courses, etc., for Royal Banquets: from August 16th, 1813 to April 23, 1828. This MS. was the work of the royal chef, and contains menus of enormous length for royal birthday dinners. At the end are 'Bills of Fare for the Banquets at the Coronation of His Majesty King George the Fourth, July the 19th, 1821'; held in Westminster Hall.

qgbnma5u.t: Recueil de quelques rem?des et m?dicamens contre diff?rentes maladies, et de plusieurs secrets et curiosit?s naturelles et chimiques.
qgbnma5u.c: Pp. 1-105, 159-end are written in a neat copper-plate hand, and are probably of the early 18th cent. Other parts are by later 18th cent. hands: there are also additions on pp. 103, 106, 146-148, dated 1888. The date 1707 occurs on p. 75: the several hands of the section pp. 107-145 seem to be of the first half of the 18th cent. P. 159 has a separate title-page: 'Secrets et curiosit?s naturelles et chimiques' and contains alchemical and chemical receipts, receipts for lacquer, etc.

qgcq7r8n.c: Collection of medical receipts, with a few cookery receipts: by several hands. A receipt 'for the Goute in the Stomach' on the verso of the 16th leaf is said to be 'Taken out of the General Evening Post Feb'y 22nd 1753'.

qgnp9wpx.t: English recipe book, 17th century and later.
qgnp9wpx.c: Collection of medical and culinary recipes in several hands.The recipes are written into a volume that was originally designed for recording classical exempla, epigrams, or extracts from Roman authors; a few entries have been made under such headings as 'Ars', 'Clementia', and 'Crudelitas'. However the volume was seemingly soon repurposed as a recipe compendium. The earliest and largest number of recipe entries are in a later 17th century hand that is also responsible for the index at the start of the volume; a few entries were made by later contributors, the latest apparently in the later 18th or even early 19th century (f. 41).Various authorities for the recipes are cited. Among the the medical ones are 'Doctor Pridgeon' [? Francis Prigeon] (f. 10); 'Doctor Lower' [Richard Lower, 1631-1691] (ff. 11, 99); 'Dr Butler' (f. 23); 'Doctr Bucanon' (f. 30); 'Docr Smith of Portsmouth' (f. 31); 'Docter Pechey' [John Pechey, d.1718] (f. 33); 'Doctor Colebatch' (f. 40); 'Dct Hunt' (f. 41); 'Doctor Windebank' [John Windebanke MD, fl.1654-1680] (f. 47); 'Doctor Dover' [Thomas Dover, d.1742] (f. 49); 'Doct Nisbit' (f. 140); 'Doctor Speers' (f. 141); 'Doctr Ross' (f. 154); 'Doctr Rosewel' [? Joh

qgq88pbk.t: A pharmocology manual. Consists of 25 chapters. The original work was written in the year 658 A.H./1259 A.D.
qgq88pbk.c: A pharmocology manual. Consists of 25 chapters. The original work was written in the year 658 A.H./1259 A.D.

qhd49dhc.c: Collection of 395 numbered, and twelve unnumbered cookery receipts in Italian. Written in a neat humanistic hand, 20 lines to a page. Ornamental initials in red with grotesque marginal decoration on ll. 13, 52, 96v, 127, 133v, 146. Other initials in red, a few black: headings in red. Fol. 1 Tabvla De La Prese/Nte Oper/A. 13 (red) Ad fare uno sciugo a una cossa de / castrato o vero spalla. c. 1?. 146 (End of numbered receipts) ... et/unge cum uno poco de zafferame / e olio: e poi lassala cocere. // Finis. 150 (End of 'A fare una substantia a uno infirmo') ... Et poi metterli / tucti queste cose in uno pignatello et / fa bollire a foco lento. The paper has a scissors water-mark, which appears to be Briquet's No. 3688, dated 1496. A name has been struck through in the upper margin of the first leaf; in the lower margin 'Joannes Christophorus Ciccurini', in a 16th cent. hand.

qjdnsyw6.t: Collection of alchemical and magical works, mainly by Ramon Lull.
qjdnsyw6.c: Collection of alchemical and magical works, mainly by Ramon LullContents1. ff. 1r-5r Ramon Lull, Accurtatiof. 1r Incipit epistola Magistri Raymondi lulii de insula mayoricarum de acurtacione lapidis benedicti missa regi roberto. In virtute sacnte trinitatis ipsiusique infinite bonitatis. Cum ego Raymundus de insula maioricarum iam preteritis temporibusm plures libros ... f. 5r ... in elementis simplicibus et compositis si ea sciveris reducere in ipsa.2. ff. 5r-7r Ramon Lull, Ars magica, chapter 3f. 5r In nomine sancte et individue trinitatis et eterne unitatis. Incipit compendium anime transmutacionis artis metallorum et lapidarie huius preciosissime artis. Composicio aque vite. Accipe Nigrum nigriusm nigro ... f. 7r ... poteris in 30 diebus lapidem componere etc. Quod potes id tempta nam operis sub pondere pressus. Subcumbat labor et frustra temptata relinquas. Nota et noli desistere quia Spiritus ubi vult spirat. Hec ars est cara levis brevisque rara.3. ff. 7v-8r Alchemical receipts4. ff. 8r-10v Pseudo-Thomas Aquinas, De lapide philosophicof. 8r Ars sancti thome de aquino brevis super philosophie et omnem in se continet virtutem. Esse suposito metalorum educitur a materia sua ...

qjtf44je.t: 1 copy of Taqwīm al-abdān fī tadbīr al-insān by Ibn Jazlah, Yaḥyá ibn ʻĪsá
qjtf44je.c: 1 copy of Taqwīm al-abdān fī tadbīr al-insān by Ibn Jazlah, Yaḥyá ibn ʻĪsá

qkebe8e5.t: Catalogues of Malayan trees, roots, herbs, fish, snakes and frogs
qkebe8e5.c: Catalogues of Malayan trees, roots, herbs, fish, snakes and frogs

qkujs5sw.c: Collection of water-colour drawings of the Constellations: with explanatory text, etc. There are 41 coloured drawings of constellations, followed by 6 astronomical figures, of which two are in colour. On the first leaf is an inscription in pencil 'E. M. E. Church St. Stoke Newington'. Produced in Stoke Newington.

qm8dy9ah.c: The anatomy of the brain explained in a series of plates. Illustrated by 12 carefully drawn and coloured plates. Watermark 1821, with printed title page dated 1823. Not obviously in Bell's hand.

qmacrhda.t: Book II of one of the most important medical manuscripts from the 10th century by Iranian physician 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas al-Majusi, written for King 'Adud al-Dawla.
qmacrhda.c: Book II of one of the most important medical manuscripts from the 10th century by Iranian physician 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas al-Majusi, written for King 'Adud al-Dawla.

qmbxnkqb.t: A composite manuscript consisting of two separate works both by Ibn Ahmad al-Qurashi.
qmbxnkqb.c: A composite manuscript consisting of two separate works both by Ibn Ahmad al-Qurashi.

qn87f9vy.c: Collection of medical receipts and prescriptions. Pp. 31/2, 41-48, 59-83, and some leaves at the end have been torn out. The pagination starts from the end of the volume. The receipts are in Latin and English, and the compiler seems to have been a physician. Pp. 91-84 contain 'Directions for preparing and administering Mrs. Stephen's Medicine for the stone in a solid form'. At the end 'D. Hartley. Feb. 10. 1745/46'. 'D. Hartley' is David Hartley the elder [1705-1757], a physician of Newark and London who was an enthusiastic supporter of Mrs. Stephen's Medicine. [See the Dictionary of National Biography]. This section is written by a different hand. Pp. 119-122 contain 'A full discovery of the Medicines given by me Joanna Stephens, for the cure of the Stone and Gravel'. This is written by the hand of the main compiler of the MS.

qpe6qmak.c: Collection of household, medical, and technical receipts. Pen-drawn diagram on p. 1 showing a method of glass-tube cutting. Produced in Norwich.

qppfff5q.c: Book of cookery receipts in French, mostly for sweetmeats, preserved fruits, etc. Written by the same hand throughout. There are also a few household receipts.

qpqazux7.c: Collection of notes on Diseases, and receipts for treatment: in English.

qq3ce8vr.c: Pharmacist's recipe book, c.1835-1840Contains recipes for pharmaceutical, cosmetic and household preparations, such as 'Pilul Antibil' (f.35v), 'Cold Cream' (f.13,) Violet Toothpowder (f.29v) and 'Black Varnish' (f.31v)Ff.55-56 contain recipes for veterinary preparations, such as 'Cleansing Drink for Cows' (f.56).Many of the recipes were obtained from other sources, and some contain reports on how effective they are, such as 'For Corns' (f.43v).

qqb2gsz9.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few medical receipts. By several hands.Followed by calligraphic examples in Arithmetic: in English. The 60 ll. at the end contain examples in arithmetic; written within red rules and embellished with pen-drawn decorations. These may possibly have been written in 1680, which is the date given in one of the examples. On the first leaf 'H. Stopes. Oct. 6, 1890.' (i.e. Henry Stopes [1852-1902], father of Marie Stopes).

qqj4f8hk.c: Proportioni overo simedrie del antico. 124 anatomical pen-drawings, with letterpress in Italian: copied from the originals of Carlo Cesi, Michael ?ngelo, Jean Cousin the Younger, and others, by Felice Ottini. The last 7 ll., which were purchased separately, are clearly part of the larger section. They contain several copies of drawings headed 'Figura anatomica di Giovanni Cusin pittore e geometro excellente in Parigi vivente nel 1593'. This is Jean Cousin, the Younger [1522-1594], author of 'Livre de pourtraicture' 1571, from which these copies have been made. The larger section contains drawings, copied from Carlo Cesi [1622-1686], Michael Angelo [1474-1564] and others. The drawings seem to have been made on odd sheets, and even on backs of letters, as in fol. 23, on the verso of which is the text of a letter dated Perugia, 18/7/1693. Unfortunately both the name of the writer and of the addressee are wanting. The letter asks for information about Giacinto Brandi [1623-1691] also a painter, and it seems to have been written by the maker of these copies to an unnamed pupil of Brandi. A fragment of the address of another letter directed to a 'Signor Giacinto' is found on the verso of

qqks252z.c: 1 copy of al-Ḥawāshī al-muḥkama ʿalā alfāẓ al-muqaddimah by Faḍālī, Sayf al-Dīn ibn ʻAṭāʼ Allāh,‏ ‎d. -1611 or 1612

qqxvanex.c: Receptes de l'onguent de Boucart, autrement dict Emplastre divin. S'ensuivent les vertus de l'onguent qui a est? faict et compos? par Monsieur du Son. Escript ? Argy le vingtneufi?me jour de Janvier I'an 1575. Cotel. On the penultimate leaf is a receipt for 'Rosolis de ma fa?on' dated 29 November 1686, signed 'C. Baron'. Written outside the upper cover 'Receptes de l'onguent de Boucart etc.', but the MS. contains particulars of Du Son's 'onguent' only. Produced in Argy.

qrdppa3y.c: The Astrologer's Guide or Magician's Companion. Written by J. T. Webb, September 1827. Author's holograph MS. Illustrated with numerous pen-drawings of geomantic figures, sigils, talismans, etc.: and with several astrological tables, of which two are folding. A work dealing with astrology, geomancy, dreams, charms, talismans, evocatory magic, etc., made up of extracts from various books on the occult sciences, some of which are named.

On the first leaf an illuminated initial A in gold and colours with marginal decoration; on the third leaf, a similar A, but without the marginal ornaments. Paragraph marks in alternate red and blue, headings in red. A booke of Medicines', below this 'Joanne Gibson. Ars longa, vita brevis. 1669', and under this 'Joanna Gibson 1708'. On the verso of the last leaf 'Liber Joannis Gibsoni Anno Domini 1632', and inside the lower cover 'Pretium 1s'.The last entry, by Joanna Gibson, is dated 1717.

qtvh85kd.c: WRIGHT, Thomas (c.1654 -?) Manuscript entitled "A Call to Repentance or a Warning before Judgement" [Circa. 1716. Dated on title page]. Thomas Wright recounts an unprovoked and seemingly mindless attack that he suffered 'in the year 1668' at the age of 14 and which left him disabled for the remainder of his life. He issues a 'Warning before Judgement' to those who have done injury to him, and to encourage 'all wicked men to leave of their boasting and Glorying of their wicked and cruel actions and to call their sins to remembrance'. Towards the end of his narrative, he describes the appalling attitudes of society towards him as a disabled man: 'I am become a scorn […] struck at me with their Cudgells others have struck me with their fists […] I am become now a prey unto the Children in the streets'. He is continually confronted with the prevailing attitudes towards disability: 'I am made to hang down my head like a bullrush and to goe heavily […] like a sparrow on the houstop which hath no mate'. This first-hand account of disability in early modern England is written by Thomas Wright at the age of 62, 48 years after the incident. Written in an easy-to-read script, the Wr

quw5r9bu.c: Bigarures. Author's holograph MS. Illustrated by numerous pen-drawn diagrams and figures, water-colour designs, sketches and symbolic pictures. The MS. is an extraordinary compilation of tracts on painting, drawing, design, horology, emblems, history-especially as regards Lorraine, etc. There are also notes on cryptography, anagrams etc.: some in Latin. Interspersed among these, are fables and pieces in verse, with many prayers and pious ejaculations-the author being apparently a victim to religious mania, and the work is one of great eccentricity throughout. Pp. 300-310 contain a genealogy of the D'Ourches family, and there are other entries on the same topic.

qvk9fu4k.c: Collection of medical, cookery and domestic receipts, by various hands: in English. The name 'Gradwell' appears on leaf 36, and 'Unkell Gradwells buns' on the next leaf. Many of the receipts are by very illiterate hands. On leaf 4v is the date 1755, and on the 16th leaf from the other end, the date 1779. There is a quotation from 'Othello' on leaf 36. The name 'James Greenhow' is found on the first fly-leaf, and on the second leaf from the end.

qvve2dt7.c: Collection of technical receipts in chemistry, also for dyes, varnishes, etc. The compiler's name and the date 1806 appear on p. 14. The 9 ll. at the end contain notes on geometry. A damaged label on the spine reads: 'Memorandums. By the late Mr. John Bennet'.

qxnbqtqj.c: Collection of cosmetic and medical receipts, with additions by different contemporary hands: in French. The folding leaf contains a receipt for 'Eau min?rale de b?zoard' by a later hand. On the verso of the last leaf 'fait par moy Octave Cholier'.

qywn5sta.c: "Cibaldone": an Italian verse translation of the third book of the 'Liber medicinalis Almansoris' on hygiene and diet. A version containing 738 lines, in three-line stanzas. At the end, a receipt for the teeth and notes on the seasons for gathering herbs, in Latin: also two short poems on diet, and on female conduct, etc. in Italian. Written in double column of 37-38 lines to a column in a semi-gothic hand. Capitals in red and black. Loose at the back of the volume are three pages on which the verse on female conduct (see f.6v lines 1-14) has been copied out neatly five times in two or possibly three different hands, at a much later date (probably 19th century). f.1, col.1 Cibaldonus.///Le oue chen de galina on de prinse Son piu generatiue e piu nutrisse/... f.5v, col.2, line 22 (End) Garofolo e caldo e seco soua natura/a stomaco e a fegato da forza/cerebro e memoria si riforza. finis. Below a receipt: Si vis semper habere pulcros dentes.f.6 Notes in Latin on the proper seasons for collecting medicinal herbs.f.6v, col.1 Verses in Italian on diet, beginning: 'Se tu doy stare sano observa questa norma'; col 2 On female conduct, verses beginning: 'Madona che dixidra esere famosa'.

r5h9tuwf.c: Collection of medical receipts, prescriptions and extracts: in English and Latin. Holograph MS. by three hands: the first, that of W. Wells [or Welles]; the second by John Symcotts; and additions by C. Haslam. On p. 77 is a pen-drawing of a distilling furnace for making 'Aqua mercurii'. The MS. is mainly the compilation by W. Wells [or Welles] and John Symcotts who appear to have been contemporaries [partners?], though entries by Symcotts usually seem to follow those of Wells. Their hands are somewhat similar but can be distinguished by the 'R' used by Wells, and the 'Z' belonging to Symcotts. Of the dated extracts the earliest is 1635 (p. 997) and the latest 1659, on a loose receipt between pp. 255 and 258. The principal Authors quoted in the MS. are Johann Hartmann [1568-1631], Sir Theodore Turquet de Mayerne [1573-1655], Oswald Crollius [1580-1609], and Lazarus Riverius [1589-1655]; all of whom were in favour of chemical remedies. Pp. 952-969 contain extracts in Latin and English by the hand of Symcotts headed 'De partu collecta ex Jaq. Guillimeau [sic]' (i.e. Jacques Guillemeau [1550-1613]).

r6fx5qkm.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few medical and household receipts. The 24 ll. at the beginning, and the 24 ll. at the end are later additions bound in. In the first of these, the dates 1818 to 1831 are found: the entries are by different hands. The main part of the text contains many additions by numerous 18th and early 19th cent. hands.

r7drdjr9.t: Watt family, Scotland, chemists: recipe and note book.
r7drdjr9.c: Small soft-cover notebook recording recipes and general notes on pharmacy, materia medica, etc. The formulae are generally medical and include (for example) medicines for epilepsy or cholera and recipes for nipple ointment or diuretics, but also include some for household compounds such as lamp black or lacquer and at least one recipe for horse medicine.At the front is an index to recipes and formulae, referring to recipes by page number. There then follows a large number of recipes and formulae, of which the initial 55 pages are numbered, written in a neat hand and referred to in the index; following this come several pages of additions in a less tidy hand, this latter section not indexed. Some recipes refer to individuals by name; it is not always clear whether these individuals are patients for whom the medicine was to be compounded, or the source of the recipe. Many of the personal names are Scottish and there is reference to Edinburgh.At the other end of the book is a section of more discursive notes on chemicals and plants, describing their medical uses: there are long sections on chloroform and cannabis.

r7g8c74v.c: A book of horse cures, by an anonymous author. ff. 3r.-15r. table of contents. ff. 15v.-17v. blank. ff. 18v.-117v. remedies in 485 chapters. ff. 117v.-118r. additional equine remedies but including an unguent for 'il mal francese'.

Some of the receipts have been smeared over in ink, among these are several charms and incantations. The compiler's name and the date are to be found on fol. 2v, at the end of a receipt 'a debelita de nervi' where he says 'per mi zinino carara aprovato in mi stesso adi 15 au[g]osto 1517'.

r9mc49ku.c: Letters to John Sloane M.D. from various correspondents, with one note to his son. Writers include John Goodsir (1814-1867), on the dissection of cholera victims. Other letters are by Lyon Playfair (1818-1898) and Jonathan Hutchinson (1828-1913).

raw347fa.c: Manuscript notes of conversations with Florence Nightingale, taken by her relative and co-worker, the poet Arthur Hugh Clough. Topics covered include God and the divine will, motherhood, Nightingale's reminiscences of her service in the Crimea, and more formal dictated material on nursing administration.

raxe965y.c: Collection of medical and veterinary receipts. The script changes from a rounded scrivener's hand (pp. 1-70) to a very illiterate variety. It is possible that the MS. was begun by a professional scribe for the compiler, and later continued in his own hand and spelling. On the last leaf verso (in the second hand) 'I was marryed to my first wiff on November 1655 bought a long hop [hoop ?] Ring cost L.1. 12s. od. Shee departted this liffe September the 26th 1676'. Pasted inside the lower cover, and written in the formal hand, 'Buriall of my wife on the 28 September 1676, the charges'. These follow, and include 19/- for a barrel of beer, 11/- for 11 quarts of wine, 10/- for a sermon, and 8/- for a 'cophin'. The total was ?4 5s. 6d. Below this in the informal hand '1632. Mistress Sarah Gree[n]away was born ye 9th of May a quter [sic] past 3 In the afternoon 1632'. 'Joseph Brooker was born ye 21st of Jun[e] 1628'. 'The bill burring [sic] my Wiff apr[il] ye 25 1704 ye parish duttys [sic] Minister & Clark & Sexton L.1.: o.: o.'. The date 1686 appears on p. 73.

rb8fn6g3.c: A continuation of Sir John Chardin's Travels to Persia and other Eastern parts. Translated into English ... and never yet published. Containing also some parts of Le Bruyn's Travels. The second volume contains Joseph Smith's armorial book-plate, where he is stated to be LL.D.

In the second part on fol. 78, there is a rough pen-drawing of 'Sant Ramon'; and on the verso of the third un-numbered leaf at the end, a crude sketch of a peacock. The date 1739 is found on the last leaf. On fol. 95 of the first section is a signature 'Albert Cirurgio de la Manrresana', written at the end of a case-history dated 1733. Three leaves at the end contain a note on 'Aygua que se anomeno Mater Balsami'. On a fly-leaf at the end, is a note by another hand of the death of Maria Albert y Grau, wife of Ramon Albert, Surgeon of Solsona, on 25 September 1782, which is probably by his hand. rg5a3rwe.c: La fleur des recettes m?dicinales. Compiler's holograph MS. Additional receipts have been written in by other and later hands, in French and Italian; an entry on the inside of the back cover is dated 1772. The title as given above is that on the spine. The date of the original MS. seems probably to have been 1674, as this is given at the end of the compiler's 'Table' where it appears twice, though in each case '5' has been written over the original '7'. It is possible, however, that the original date has been altered to 1654 so as to fit the entry referring to Nicaise Lef?vre's Traict? de la chimie which is given that date in Le Gay's table of contents, where it is the eighth section of the MS. In his title-page Le Gay calls this MS. 'Livre ou manuscript dans lequel sont descriptes plusieurs belles receptes contre toutes les maladies ... et d'autres tr?s curieuses, le tout tir? de divers manuscripts, de plusieurs doctes personnes ... de tr? bons autheurs...' Premi?re partie: Receptes contre toutes sortes de fi?vres. Seconde partie: Des maux de poitrine ... la petite v?role, vers des petits enfans. rguc3pu9.t: Alphabetical glossary of drugs and their properties.
rguc3pu9.c: Alphabetical glossary of drugs and their propertiesA very neatly written manuscript in a bold uncial hand with marginalia. The first folio is a leaf taken from another manuscript to serve as a cover. This odd leaf is rubricated, but there are no rubrics in the main text, nor any illuminations, black ink only being employed. There is no title, nor any indication of the writer's identity, but the script, spelling and composition of the manuscript all point to the late fifteenth century as its date. (The Saxon forms of some of the letters are retained, especially r and f.) The volume contains two separate compositions, but the whole is the work of one scribe, the second composition follows the first without break. There are some few marginal annotations in an Elizabethan handwriting.Contentsf. 1r-v pastedown, not part of original work1. f. 2r- v An alphabetical list of drugs (plants and minerals) in Latin, with the English equivalents inserted in many casesThe beginning of this is lost; the surviving portion contains the letters S (part), T, V and Z.2. ff. 2v-56v An alphabetical glossary of drugs (mostly plants) and their propertiesThis is preceded by an introductory paragraph beginni

On p. 91 is a Revolutionary song 'Les travaux d'Hercule r?alis?s par les parisiens' dated 1789: there are other verses on pp. 151, 164. P. 166, of which only the inner half remains, contains pen-drawn circular figures, which possibly illustrate the parts of a clock, but there seems to be no related text. There are many receipts for artificial gems, dyes, varnishes, etc.

s3rkhn4x.c: A parchment and paper manuscript copy of the Livre des simples médecines , i.e. the French adaptation of the Circa instans attributed to Platearius, followed by a collection of recipes and a medical glossary in French, with additions of recipes in Latin and French by contemporary or slightly later readers on blanks, including one recipe mentioning Berthe&#769lemy (Medici) Mye, recipes by Simon of Pavia, Louis Abraham, Pierre de Gre&#768ce, Pantaleone Confienza, Jean de la Planche, Jean Espiart [or Espiard], Johannes de Scala, and the unidentified barbers/physicians G. Fabert and A. Bruneti, recipes for Charles the Bold and Jean de Bourbon, abbot of Cluny, and the verse entitled Virtutes Agnus Dei . Written and illustrated in Northern France (French Flanders or Picardy), c. 1470. Contents : 1. ff. 1r-261r, Livre des simples me&#769decines , the French adaptation of the late 12th-century pharmaceutical treatise in Latin known as Circa instans attributed to a physician operating in the milieu of the School of Salerno, named as Platearius. s8eutkmm.t: Carr, Sir Rochester (d. c.1695), 5th Bart; lunatic.
s8eutkmm.c: Documents relating to the administration of the estate of Sir Rochester Carr, younger son of Sir Edward Carr (d. 1618). Rochester Carr had been declared a lunatic in 1637. The documents comprise annual accounts of John Burslem, who was responsible for collecting the lunatic's revenues and paying his maintenance, with supporting documentation, submitted to the Lord Chancellor.

At the end are some short articles on special topics: Pp. 117-198 Trattato de vini. 199-204 Trattato de gl'aceti. 205-216 Trattato di far varie sorte de pane et altre cose da magnare [sic]. 217-228 Trattato di pigliar i pesci [et] ogni sorte di ucelli. There are some additions by somewhat later hands.

sa46pm4v.c: Via veritatis ... von der Quinta Essentia und Oleo Metallorum. Sowohl aus deren Metallen als auch aus deren Mineralien deutlich und Klahr beschrieben. Wie auch darneben von vielen geheimen Arzneyen so ich auf meiner Wallfarth erhalten und auch richtig befunden habe. Beschrieben von mir St. Petri Closter. Anno Domini 1480. Illustrated with 11 crude water-colours symbolizing alchemical processes, and two pen-drawings of alchemical apparatus (fol. 16, fol. 91). Inserted are two engraved silhouette portraits of the head of Susanna Catharina von Klettenberg [1723-1774], the friend of Goethe, and various holograph notes on Basilius Valentinus, etc. by Heinrich Lemperts Senior [1816-1898], the art collector and bookseller, dated 1896, who has also written on a title-slip pasted on the spine, 'Goethe's Exemplar. Vgl. Ausg. d. Werken 1840. Bd. XXI s. 152-159'. Other notes by him are dated 1891. Written inside the lower cover 'Zeidlers Land Ministerium'. This is possibly Karl Sebastian Zeidler, Rathssekretar at N?remberg [1719-1786], and not Johann Heinrich Zeidler [1706-1760] the compiler of the 'Universal Lexicon'.

samzrcda.c: Gemma secretorum sive Antidotarium speciale et quasi miraculosum. Recollectum, a Patre Eusebio Matisconensi Capucino: in French. Author's holograph MS. The title, preface, heading and some of the formulae are in Latin, but the text is in French. On p. 82 is the date 1734, and on p. 244, the date 1739; both of these seem to have been later additions. On p. 212 the date 1732 appears in the text. The volume contains miscellaneous medical receipts, many of them made up from chemical substances, cosmetical receipts, etc. Text mostly within red crayon rules.

sb4ha69n.c: Collection of medical and cookery receipts, by various hands. The second leaf bears the date 1669, but some of the receipts are probably later: the main hand writes in an illiterate script. The volume seems to have been used as a Memorandum book of a jeweller and/or money-lender, as 7 of the last 12 leaves at the end contain notes of plate and jewels pledged, dated 1638-42. Among these is an entry of a loan of ?200 on 'a great dimond ringe' to Sir Matthew Lister in 1641. This would be the physician to Anne, wife of James, I, and later to Charles I, who knighted him in 1636. He was born in 1564 and died in 1656, aged 92.

sb36brek.c: Mainly cookery and domestic receipts, with a few medical entries. The entries are by several hands, one towards the end 'Cheese from potatoes' is dated 1838. A receipt for tomato sauce is pasted inside the upper cover, and one for preserving cucumbers signed 'Fanny Peacocke 1830' is pasted down on the last leaf.

Almost all the receipts, etc. are in French, but there are a few in English. The last nine pages (Nos. 1366-1374) contain two drafts and an English translation by D'?on, of a description of a: 'Grille ?conomique', designed to save coal in fire-places. At the end he gives his address: 'Mdlle D'?con, No. 38 Brewer St. Golden Square [London]'. P. 46 is a holograph letter, dated London, 19/7/1791 from Madame Dauberval, enclosing a printed broadside 'M?thode pour prendre le kina dans les fi?vres'. In reference to this on p. 48 D'?on has written: 'Bonne lettre de Madame Dauberval ... Bonne ? employer et ? mettre ? la t?te de l'?dition de l'ouvrage suivant que je me propose de donner au public. sgrkn9s9.t: Sarah Tully, Lady Hoare [and others]: "Book of Receipts for Cookery and Pastry & c".
sgrkn9s9.c: "Book of Receipts for Cookery and Pastry 1732 & c.": pencilled signature of Sarah Tully, Lady Hoare. Indexed The volume is continued in several different hands. Some Indian connection is suggested by recipes for "kebobs" '"pilau", "currie powder" and there is some evidence for European travel or contacts. Pasted to the inside front cover: Unrecorded advertising broadside, printed in English in Venice, for the famous theriaca fina or Venice treacle, a honey- or molasses-based composition thought efficacious against poisoning, sold at the "Aquila Nera" [At the Sign of the Blak Eagle] in the Merceria San Salvatore. Various later 17th or early 18th century hands have entered further recipes from the back of the volume. One hand has recorded the following prescriptions: 'Dr Paxton's dirrections for Frank for the eye water' (f. 38), 'an electuary for costiveness by Dr Frewin' (f. 39), 'the quieting draught ordered by Sir Ed. Harris for Frank to take after Physick' (f. 44), 'a Receipt for the Collick ordered by Dr Keill, for one of my servants' (f. 46v.), and 'an other-reciet for the scurvy, ordered for Sir Harry Tyrrell' (f. 47v.). sx2nv9yd.c: Household cookery book which also includes some medical recipes, mainly located towards the back of the volume. Written in several hands, with an index located at the front, although not all the recipes are included in the index. There seems to have been an attempt to arrange the recipes by subject, but this was clearly abandoned at some point. A large number of recipes involve the use of fruit, particularly apricots, cherries and gooseberries. A few miscellaneous notes have been made throughout the volume, including a short poem underneath a recipe for 'Leek' on f. 79r, and a list of 'the vertues' of 'The Lady Allen's Water,' a treatment for plague, smallpox and all other infectious diseases, on f.157r. Folios, 20, 49-52, 80-83, 96, 171, 176-179, 182-187 and 208 are all blank.

t8nec94v.c: Herbario nuovo, con discorsi che dimostrano li nomi, la specie, la forma, il loco, il tempo, le qualit?, e le virt?- mirabili dell'herbe, insieme col peso, et ordine d'usarle, scuoprendo rari secreti e singolari rimedii da sanare le piu difficili infirmita del corpo humano. The title is that of Durante's 'Herbario nuovo' first published in Rome in 1585, but this MS. contains only the plants from 'Abrotano' to 'Aro maggiore'. The remainder of the text consists of medical and alchemical receipts and 'secrets'. The last two leaves have entries by a later hand, and the date 1796 is found on the last page.

t35pw22x.c: With an 'Abschrift des 'Rosarium Philosophorum' gefertigt Januar 1903, durch Dr. Carl Gerster zu Braunfels.' Illustrated with pen-drawings of alchemical apparatus on fol. 3v, and on fol 42v in the second part, and of a poultice on fol. 129. Some marginal and interlinear corrections and additions in red ink by a later 16th cent. hand. The second work, which has been written on blank leaves of the original MS., is a transcript of the second volume of the collection of alchemical tracts published at Frankfort by Cyriacus Jacobus in 1550, under the title 'De alchimia opuscula complura veterum philosophorum'. Dr. Gerster has pasted in pen-drawn copies of the t.p. and woodcut illustrations of the original, done on tracing paper.

t37je3ma.t: Collection of medical recipes, in Latin, partly following the arrangement of chapters in Rhazes, Liber nonus ad Almansorem, and partly extracted from Bartolomeo da Montagnana, Antidotarium.
t37je3ma.c: A collection of recipes, in Latin, written by two hands, probably in North East Italy, mid 15th century. The collection follows the usual head to toe arrangement in medieval medical manuals and, in particular, in the Liber nonus ad Almansorem, a treatise on the medical therapy of diseases written by the Persian physician Muhammad ibn Zakariya al-Razi (865-925 or 933), known in the West as Rhazes or Rhasis. Additional recipes added at the end of the volume by contemporary hands include excerpts from the Antidotarium of the Paduan physician Bartolomeo da Montagnana (c. 1380-before Feb. 1452).Contents1. ff. 1r-30v: Receptarium, in Latin, partly drawing from Rhazes, Liber nonus ad Almansorem, in the Latin translation attributed to Gerardus of Cremona (1114-1187). The manuscript was formerly identified (Moorat, I, p. 509) as an abridged copy of the Latin translation of Rhazes's work because of the similarities in the chapter titles and beginnings with those in the parallel chapters by Rhazes in the edition produced at Milan by Leonardus Pachel and Uldericus Scinzenzeler, dated 14 Feb. 1481, ff. i7r-m3v (ISTC ir00175000).The incipit 'Soda est lesio in membris capitis' of the first chapte

t58cm5u3.c: Les secres de Madame la pr?sidente de Maliverny pour plusieurs mox. Tomme segont. By several hands, one of which is very illiterate. It is apparently a continuation of MS. No. 3409, and is partly by the same hands. There are a few magical remedies. Produced in Aix?

t73s6mm3.c: Manuscript containing domestic / culinary recipes, with calligraphic ownership statement, Mary Hawker, inscribed on inner leave along with the date 1691. No further details about Mary Hawker are known. The volume is 16 x 22 cms and 26 pages in total; as well as some additional loose recipe papers folded within the manuscript. It also contains examples of early shorthand, and there seems to be another hand within the volume. Towards the reverse of the volume, there are household guidelines and instructions, such as how to remove stains from silk. Folder 2 contains papers about the manuscript, including correspondence with record offices about the manuscript, and a document titled "Mary Hawker - her book, 1691" which was a (mostly fictionalised) account of Mary's life written by the donor's borther. Also includes the envelope that the volume was contained in since c. 1980s. A partial transcription of the shorthand created by a researcher is saved in the collection file.

tc33fm3w.c: By an anonymous German alchemist who claims to have discovered the Method and Praxis of the Philosopher's Stone after fifteen years of labour and research. P. 17 Descriptio Athanaris [sic] mei. 19, 20 Introduction, in which the Author tells of his 15 years labours and ultimate success, ending: 'Ich die klar Beschreibung des gantzens Wercks durch unterschiedene Modos ausero setze, und dir auss Vatterlicher Liebe loco legati hinterlassen wollen'. 21 Copy of a letter from Paracelsus. 22 Via sicca brevis: in Latin. 23 Via humida longa: in Latin. 29 Von der Beschaftigheit der Materi. 65 Die Klare Praxis. 92 Secretissima Instructio ad Lapidem pro via sicca et humida: in German. 130 Via universalis ad Lapidem: in German. 144 Wo und an welchen die Materi am bestem zufinden sey. An account of various minerals and substances, and of the mines and other places where they are found-mostly in Central Europe. This section is divided into 170 paragraphs, and some of the entries of the author's travels are dated between 1662 (p. 152)

tcefzdg4.c: Collection of medical and cookery receipts in various hands, later 17th century - c. 1800. The latter recipes are largely arranged in alphabetical order from the back. There is an acephalous index to both sections at the front of the book (ff. 1-17). Authorities cited include Sir Kenelm Digby (f. n135v.), 'Dr Bryan' (f. 158v.), 'Dr Chambers' (f. 118 r.), 'Dr Nursse' (f. 129r.) [?Thomas Nurse MD, c. 1598-1667], and 'Dr. Sermon' (f. 136r.) tf8zdh6u.c: Collection of texts relating to astrology by Albumasar, John of Seville and Ibn al-Saffar, in Latin, copied by the unidentified surgeon Guidotus of Vicenza in Northern Italy; with decorated initials and rubrication.Contents (described according to the more recent modern foliation; earlier foliation recorded in brackets):f. iiir: Table of Properties in five columns, 14th century.f. iiiv: List of contents in the hand of Tomaso Balena, 16th century.1) ff. 5r-78v (formerly 3r-68v): Albumasar (Abu Ma'shar Ja'far; d. 886), Maius introductorium in scientia astrorum, translated from Arabic into Latin by John of Seville (Iohannes Hispalensis; active in Portugal in the 1120s and 1130s, and possibly in Toledo in the 1140s-1150s).The Great Introduction to Astrology is the most important work of Albumasar, the best-known astrologer of the Middle Ages, born of Persian descent in Balkh (in modern Afghanistan), but active in Baghdad (in modern Iraq) for most of his life. The text is divided into eight books and provides a detailed description and defence of astrology as a scientific subject within the framework of Aristotelian natural philosophy. tsu67jcn.c: Ars algebra et analytica ac alma cabula. MDCLXXX: in German. A work of cabbalistic alchemy in prose and verse by a Dresden apothecary. Illustrated by many remarkable wash drawings, symbolic emblems, and pictures in red chalk. At the end are copies of various documents, orders from, and petitions to Johann Georg II, Elector of Saxony [1656-1680], one of which gives the author permission to search for metals. On the title given above is the date 1680, but near the beginning of the work is a mention of Elector Johann Georg III [d. 1691] and of Elector Johann Georg IV [d. 1694], the latter apparently still being alive; hence the MS. seems to have been written 1691-1694. tuxwa2nw.c: Receipts copied from Miss Myddleton's Book, August 15th, 1785. With many added receipts for remedies by various later hands, extracts, and pasted-in cuttings from newspapers, etc. On p. 100 of the first book is an extract, copied from the 'Chelmsford Chronicle', September 1818. The receipts are entirely medical; the first 6 ll. consist of an index to both parts.

tvav3nvp.c: "A continuation of Sir John Chardin's Travels to Persia and other Eastern parts. Translated into English ... and never yet published. Containing also some parts of Le Bruyn's Travels." Though the title is as given above, and the spines of both volumes are lettered "Sir John Chardin's Travels continu'd", all except the first 40 ff. of the first volume is devoted to Bruin's Travels. These 40 ff. contain Chardin's first journey from Ispahan to Bander Abassi. This started on January 1st 1674, but in this MS. the narrative stops at the middle of the entry for February 12 of that year. This is followed by "The travels of Cornelius le Brun through Muscovy and Persia to the East Indys, the coast of Malabar, the Island of Ceylon, Batavia, Bantam and other places": chapters 50 to the beginning of Chapter 68 (140 ff.). The rest of Vol.1 consists of Chapters 15 and 16 of the same work written by another hand. Bruin's Journeys are dated 1703-1706. On the first leaf of Vol. 1 is the signature of Joseph Smith. The first 40 ff. of Vol. 1 and the following 140 ff. of this volume are written apparently by Joseph Smith himself.

tvb96dcm.c: Collection of cookery and household receipts: with additions by other hands. Some additional receipts by various hands have been inserted. 'Sarah Ellis, Mansfield' is inscribed in pencil on the first leaf. Produced in Mansfield.

tvwpbqzg.c: Recueil de recettes; mainly in French, but with some entries in German, and a few additions by other hands. The main collection contains a few veterinary receipts, and the other section (29 pp.), beginning at the other end of the volume, consists of miscellaneous receipts. Produced in Sur.

tw557grr.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few medical and household receipts: written by various hands. Some of the receipts are dated, the earliest 1810 (third leaf from the end), and the latest 1838 (p. 152).

ty88uu2k.c: Tr?sor de sant?. Partly Compiler's holograph MS. Below the date on the title-page is 'dor? scrips[it]', and the MS. seems to have been partly written by him, and partly by Madame Lievain herself. The latest dated entry, 1740, is found on the fifth leaf. The second leaf from the end is inscribed 'Extrait de la Naissance des enfants de Mme Lievain' in the scribal hand, but some of the entires are by her hand. Between 1712 and 1727 she gave birth to five sons and five daughters, of whom all survived except a son born in 1717 who lived only four months. The receipts are mainly medical, but include also a few for conserves, essences, etc.

tza9ctm3.c: Comprises Mūǧiz al-Qānūn (Abstract of Avicenna's Canon) by Alā' ad-Dīn ̀Alī b. abī l-Ḥazmal-Qurašī, known as Ibn an-Nafīs.

u3s7cvf7.c: Collection of 14 manuscripts containing medical, cookery and other receipts; by various 17th and 18th cent. hands: mainly in English, but with some entries in Latin and French. Some of the MSS. are incomplete as noted below.

u3zmchfs.c: Collection of medical, veterinary and cookery receipts: by several hands.pp. 1-16 of the second part, and some leaves at the beginning of the first part wanting. This MS. is made up of two separate volumes bound together, probably in the 18th century. The first volume is almost entirely by the same hand, and seems to have been compiled by a Mrs Meade, as she speaks of remedies for an infant Nathanael Meade, who is perhaps the Sir Nath. Meade, Serjeant-at-Law, who died in 1760, as recorded in Musgrave. Many receipts in this volume are assigned to 'Dr. Thomas Lower'. It seems most probable that this is the Quaker brother of the more famous Richard Lower [1631-1691]. In the D.N.B. entry for Thomas Lower [1633-1720] 'Quaker sufferer', it is stated that he had qualified as a physician, and had perhaps practised in London. The second volume - the first 16 pp. of which are missing - begins with a receipt dated 1717, and contains another dated 1727 (p. 149). It is also written by several different hands.

u5zfvgck.c: Receipt book [probably Irish], containing a mixture of culinary, medical, veterinary and household recipes in a number of different hands. Sporadic dated material in the volume indicates that the majority of contents were entered between c.1780 and c.1814. The creators are not known: this volume has passed through many hands and had various authors.Contents are not separated by type of receipt, however the first 15 folios are mainly medical receipts and the remainder up to f.154v are culinary and household with the odd medical receipt on f.80r, f.81r and f.124r. The contents of ff.155r-176v are a mixture of medical, culinary and household receipts. Receipts have been entered from the 'reverse' of the volume starting at f.170r and ending at f.156v .The culinary receipts are dominated by ones for cakes, puddings, creams and jellies and many are included several times, with variations and in different hands, notably, for example, receipts for plum cake. As well as plums, there are several receipts for lemon cakes, cream cheeses, almond pastries, oysters and various pickles (including a receipt for Indian pickles "how to pickle colliflowers, cabbages, raddish, kidney beans, asparagus,

u9ujczvz.c: "A Booke of divers receipts." Many of the receipts are for 'Waters', and a few for cookery.After fol. 36 some different hands are found, the latest dated entry being 1744 (fol. 51v). On fol. 34 is the end of a receipt for 'The Earl of Strafords [sic] Gout Water', where the compiler states: 'I had this receipt of Sir George Wentworth who did highly praise it...' This gentleman was M.P. for Pontefract in 1640 but was disabled from sitting for his loyalty to Charles I, who later conferred a knighthood upon him and made him general of the royalist forces in Ireland. He died in 1660, aged 60. At the bottom of fol. 35 'I had this receipt [A 'cleansing water for the skinne'] of Mrs. Dorothy Osburne [1627-1695] now Sr. Wm. Temples Lady'. She married in 1655.

u36qxg6x.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few medical and domestic receipts: by several hands. The date 1844 is found on one of the unnumbered leaves. Inscribed on the lower cover in pencil: 'Doctor A. B. Evans Collection' (i.e. Arthur Benoni Evans [1781-1854], miscellaneous writer [see the Dictionary of National Biography]).

u43qhup6.c: Written in a neat humanistic hand. Illustrated with 38 well executed pen drawings of constellations, etc., the stars in red. The manuscript is foliated 120r-153v, so it was originally part of a larger work. The illustrations are mostly in the style of the printed editions of Manilius, Hyginus and Aratus.f. 121r Aetherios orbis, subiectaque templa deorum / Musa cane, atque uias semper uoluentis olimpi / ... 153v Qui nunc astrorum motus subiectaque diuum / Templa cano atque uias semper uoluentes olimpi.

ua3c24xd.c: Recipe book of Lady Ann Fanshawe, wife of Sir Richard Fanshawe (1608-1666), English ambassador to Spain, containing medical, culinary and other recipes, compiled from 1651. With additional entries in various later hands. The earliest entries are in the hand of one Joseph Averie, presumably a clerk acting as Ann Fanshawe's amanuensis, although most are signed by the latter. Many are ascribed to 'my mother' [Margaret Fanshawe], other members of the extended Fanshawe family, Sir Kenelm Digby, and others. Some of the recipes appear to be in Ann Fanshawe's own hand, a few are Spanish, dated Madrid, 1664-65. f. 2r. 'K[atherine] Fanshawe. Given mee by my Mother March 23th 1678'.f. 3r. 'Mrs Fanshawes Booke of Receipts of Physickes, Salves, Waters, Cordialls, Preserves and Cookery written the eleventh day of December 1651 by Me, Joseph Averie'.ff. 4r.-16v. medical recipes in various hands.ff. 17r.-29v. largely blank, but with some later, barely legible scribbles and a rough sketch of a flower at ff. 18-19.ff. 30r.-37v. further medical recipes.ff. 38r.-52v. blank.ff. 53r.-54r. rough sketches by the same hand as at ff. 18-19.ff. 54v.-56v. blank.ff. 57r.-v. additional medical recipes copied by

ua87equq.c: Called Kitab-i viladat-i Iskandar - 'The book of birth of Iskandar' or 'Iskandar horoscope' - this manuscript contains the horosocope of a Timurid prince, Iskandar Sultan. Personal horoscopes were quite common in the medieval Middle East, but this one is one of the finest examples of its kind. Written in 1411 by the court astrologer of Iskandar Sultan.

ucmk8bm2.c: 17th and 18th century English recipe book comprising culinary receipts, along with a small amount of medical receipts, in several hands.Divided into two sections, both indexed. The front of the book contains medical receipts. The index to this section is preceded by a page laying out apothecary marks and other abbreviations. The back section contains culinary receipts. Includes "Directions for ye use of medicines in a physick chest, fitt for travelling by sea or Land" (p. 117)Medical receipts are followed by a "Corect list of Every thing in season in every month in the year" and a few further culinary recipes. A few loose recipes inserted at the beginning of this section.The two sections of the book are opposite ways up, each working inwards from a cover that it treats as the "front".

ucs9s7eq.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with some medical receipts. Written mainly by two hands, one of which may be that of Lady Catherine Fitzgerald.

udax4qtm.c: Books 1 and 2 of Tadhkirat ʾulī-l-albāb wa-l-jāmiʿ li-l-ʿajab-l-ʿujāb

udc93tjt.c: A translated extract of Avicenna's Canon of Medicine.

udm6vxpb.c: Medical case-book: in English. Written in a school-boy's arithmetic exercise-book, in which the name Alexander Morgan is found twice with calligraphic decorations, on the first leaf, and on the verso of the last. He is apparently the writer of these medical notes on patients; the name is also found, written in a more mature hand, in the top outer corner inside the upper cover. The earliest dated entry is 1720 on p. 15, and in several of the previous cases, the writer speaks of 'my master'; he was probably then a student apprentice. An approximate date for the earliest entries may be deduced from that on p. 6, which describes the case of a man 'who on the Coronation day received a wound'. This must refer to the Coronation of George I in 1714. The latest date is 29 August 1747 on the fifth preliminary unnumbered leaf.

uerzw4wq.c: Collection of medical receipts in alphabetical order of diseases; at the end some cookery and miscellaneous receipts: in Italin and Latin. There are some added receipts by later hands, one of which is dated 1732. On the fifth leaf of the last section, at the end of a receipt for 'Pulvis Cornac[c]-hini', is a note 'Scribebat hoc pro Amico (nempe Burattino) Joannes Baptista. dezima hora. die 27 Martii 1650'. Many of the receipts have the names of their authors added, who are mainly late 16th cent. and early 17th cent. Physicians. On the verso of the last leaf, and in the lower margin of other leaves, are the intials H.B.

uf5f2nzq.c: Collection of medical receipts and remedies in English. The text ends: 'Finutur [sic] die Feb. 19, 8.30 p.m. 1657. For W. Coleman per W.C. out of the originall of a deceased Chymist and Physitian being brother in law to W. Coleman'. On the verso of the first leaf are some astronomical notes dated 1664, 1665.

ug4dxmfe.c: Magia de profundis, seu Clavicula Solomonis regis Lib. IV. The Key of Solomon the King. Or a compleat system of profound magical science. Fred. Hockley scrip[sit]. Most of the illustrations are unfinished and uncoloured: the text also is incomplete. The paper is water-marked '1826 Sweetapple'.

ug8t4yqh.c: Lucy Culley's Receipt Book. A collection of cookery, medical and household receipts, with additions by numerous hands. Only the first two leaves are by the original compiler. William Paul whose name appears on the verso of fol. 9, with date 1794, seems to have written the receipts as far as the 33rd leaf. These are followed by various receipts by different hands, the latest of which on the verso of fol. 53 is dated 1858. There are 14 inserted receipts by various 19th cent. hands pasted in after fol. 54.

ug24vw3b.t: Compendium rarissimum totius Artis Magicae sistematisatae per celeberrimos Artis hujus Magistros. Anno 1057. Noli me tangere.
ug24vw3b.c: In German and Latin. On white, brown and grey-green paper. The title within an ornamental border in wash, with skulls, skeletons and cross-bones. Illustrated with 31 extraordinary water-colour drawings of demons, and three pages of magical and cabbalistic signs and sigils, etc. At the end the figures are in red, and part of the text is written in white on the grey-green paper.

ugn23v6p.c: Collection of alchemical, and other receipts for making artificial metals and gems, dyes and tinctures, etc. With directions for making alchemical medicine, quintessences, distillations etc.; Written in a neat rounded gothic hand: 20 lines to a page. The text is surrounded by an ornamental border with floral motif: in the lower margin two Cupids and the sacred monogram IHS in gold on a blue ground. There are 12 carefully executed pen-drawings of alchemical apparatus. uh667msg.c: Le soleil terrifi? par l'art m?tallique. M?thodiquement traitt? [sic] par un Amateur de la V?rit?. En debes pulchra ferundo scire. Per anagramma Fredericus Conderus ab Helpen. 1689. Author's holograph MS. Facing the title, is a second title: 'Aurea pluvia Jovis. F. C. ab Helpen ou de Secour [sic]. Ex auctoribus plurimis collecta Parisiis. 1689. La Pluye d'Or de Jupiter'. On the first preliminary leaf is a numerical 'Alphabetum Kaballisticum', and below this in capital letters 'Fredericus Conderus ab Helpen'. The work is a kind of alchemical encyclopaedia in 29 chapters, made up from extracts in Latin and French from the writings of a very large number of alchemical authors of all periods. It is apparently unrecorded. Produced in Paris.

uhfezp9t.c: Collection of veterinary receipts, etc.: in German. The section from the beginning to fol. 104 contains 75 full-page water colour drawings of bits, bridles, etc., a stable, illustrations of horse training, one of which (fol. 27) is folding: these are mostly signed 'F' and include a picture showing the administration of a medicine by means of a funnel (fol. 31), and another of blood-letting (fol. 29). The original compiler's work ends at fol. 281, and contains 1160 numbered receipts: it is followed by additions by several hands, inserted receipts, etc. On fol. 3 and on the fly-leaf at the beginning the name 'Von Kupperwolff' has been stamped.

ukase86f.c: On pp. 149, 150 occur the words 'approved by me Abigail Smith' and elsewhere 'probatum A.S.' This MS. is therefore catalogued under SMITH (Abigail). On the first leaf, a 19th cent. owner has written 'Miss Dorothy Bate's Cookery and Receipt Book ... 1697-1763'. Though the name Dorothy Bate [or Pate] occurs in the MS. she does not seem to have been the compiler. As to the first date 1697, this is apparently taken from some leaf of the MS. now lost. The main text ends at p. 175, and is followed by receipts written by various hands of the first half of the 18th cent., one of the verso of the 5th unpaginated leaf is dated 1763.

On fol. 5v is a 'Benedictio seu exorcismus contra tempestatem et turbinem, approbata et confirmata ex veteri Rituali loci Bauceti descripto Anno 1694'. Produced in Les Baux.

umxzha5m.c: Collection of recipes, mainly medical, in formula format with precise ingredient measurements; for ointments, salves, balsams, tonics, waters, beers, spirits, wines, unctions, powders, cordials, "balls" (pills), syrups, elixirs, lozenges and diuretics. Many do not recommend a specific ailment for which they should be used to treat. Includes some veterinary recipes, "beast medicines" particularly for sick and calving cows, (pp.80-84, 101-102); household recipes for inks, waxes, varnish, herb tobacco (p.72), polishes, blacking, dyes, washing powder, glue, soaps, hair powder and bathing liquids; recipes for gin, brandy and gooseberry champaigne (p.127) and walnut ketchup (p.106-107); and something called the "Whitworth Diet Drink" (p.128) Recipes are written in the same hand up to p.107, thereafter it is in various different hands. Some recipe titles are in Latin form. An inscription has been scratched off on the inside front cover, and there are no other indications of ownership. In between pp.62-63 is a loose piece of paper with 5 ingredients written on it. No date, circa early 19th century. Contains comprehensive index at front of volume.1 volume: 113 x 185 mm., 132ff. unpytw58.c: Medical/cookery recipe book, with recipes written by Lady Pulston, pp.45-74. Some pages appear to be missing; the first page of the MSS is numbered page 45. Pages 57-62 are torn from the top left to bottom right corner, rendering some text illegible. A number of the recipes include the notation "proved". Includes recipes from other individuals, commonly Lady Parsons. Examples of medical recipes: "for the bileing of a snake or any venemous thing: Lady Parsons"; "for the toothach"; "the plague water: Lady Parsons"; "to kill dead flesh"; "an excellent scarcloth: Lady Heath"; "for the scurvey".

urjngqzk.c: Collection of medical, veterinary and household recipes, apparently compiled by a Devonshire medical practitioner from 1776 to c.1781. With additional medical related entries, including (ff. 56v.-57v) 'directions for a sea box'. Numerous Devon medical figures are mentioned in the text, including Dr Huxham (ff. 1r, 43v), Dr Downman (f. 50v.) and Dr Harvey (f. 62v recipe dated 28 July 1779).

usbf5e3d.c: Manual on pregnancy and childcare, compiled by Maria Rundell, with various remedies for pregnant women and for children, The Retreat, 17 Oct. 1810. The work seems to have been written for a daughter, Harriet, about whom nothing is known. There is no evidence of publication. f. 1r.-v. remedies for whooping cough and ringworm. ff. 2r.-41r. observations and advice on pregnancy, childbirth and care of the new-born (with a sketch of an infant's napkin, f. 17r.). ff. 41v.-52v. remedies for pregnant and lying-in women. ff. 52v.-53r. weaning of infants. f. 53r. memorandum on the 'turn of life'. ff. 53v.-73r. observations and advice on the care of children. ff. 73v.-back cover index. Additional remedies inside front and back covers, with a recipe for 'plain pap', dated Pisa 6 Jan. 1828 (the year of Mrs Rundell's death), in an enclosure affixed to the back cover.

ut5j9bdn.t: Manuscript recipe book of Grace Carteret, 1st Countess Granville (1654-1744).
ut5j9bdn.c: English manuscript book of medicinal and culinary recipes owned by Grace Carteret, 1st Countess Granville (1654-1744), with ownership inscription on the inside front cover. The volume is closely associated with the contemporary Ann Fanshawe recipe manuscript held by the Wellcome Library (MS.7113). The Carterets and Fanshawes were family friends, as Ann Fanshawe's memoirs ( British Library Add MS 41161 ) indicate. The families' relationship is reflected in overlaps in content between the recipes in the two volumes, notably the highly unusual early recipe for ice cream at MS.8903, f.9. This is closely related to the famous ice cream recipe at MS.7113, f.158r, and appears to date to before the first English printed ice cream recipe in Mrs. Mary Eale's Receipts (London 1718).The recipes are undated but the majority are written in a single fair hand dating from the mid to late 17th century, with additional recipes added or inserted in a wide variety of hands dating to around the mid 18th century. uu2mt3hc.c: [Receipts for] kitchen and household use, some 100 years old in the Matthey and Goodall Families. Written by various hands from about 1750 to 1900, which is the date of a pencilled note on the treatment of boils on fol. 111. This is intialled 'E.M.' (i.e. Edward Matthey [1837-1918]) and dated 9/12/1900. The receipts at the beginning are mostly cookery receipts, but those from fol. 70 onwards are medical. There are numerous inserted receipts by different hands, both cookery and medical, many pasted in. Among those on fol. 50 is an estimate, dated 1 February, 1866, sent in by H. Chaplin, cook and confectioner of 2 Upper Baker St., London, for the wedding breakfast for Marie Matthey. It involved a meal for 24 persons at 12/6 per head, without wine. The title given above is from a label pasted on to the spine, and written by Edward Matthey: the upper part is missing.

uufnejnn.c: Segreti bellissimi. The receipts are not only medical, but also for household and technical purposes.

Among the medical receipts is one dated 1640, and on a fly-leaf at the end is an account dated 1686. The MS. is written by several different hands.

v495u8s2.c: Charms and demonology. Though the term "demonology" is used in the manuscript itself, the creatures being described are known in Malay as "hantu", which differs from the Western conception of demons in that the term is commonly used to describe spirits and mythological creatures in general, both malicious and not. Though some may also be called demons or syaitan in the Islamic sense, not all hantu are necessarily demonic.

Caillet also mentions a biography by Millet de Saint Pierre published at Le Havre in 1859 under the title of 'Recherches sur le dernier sorcier'.

vfgmemz5.c: Collection of cookery receipts, with a few medical and household receipts: and some additions by later hands. On the verso of the first leaf: 'Amy Eyton her Book pris 2s'. On the recto of the same leaf she has written: 'A note of my Close Desem 19, 1691', followed by a list of garments. A Mary Eyton also seems to have owned the book as she has written inside the upper cover: 'Mary Eyton her Book', and inscribed her name on the inside of the lower cover. The Eyton entries are in a very illiterate hand, with remarkable orthography. On the 22nd leaf, starting from the other end of the volume is a medical receipt to cure cancer by means of powdered corns from a gelded horse: this is dated 1738. The name of 'Mrs Sarah Justice' is found on the last leaf.Please note that this item is in a fragile condition and must be handled with care. Researchers are requested to view the online digital version or microfilm version in the first instance.

vfssjr4s.c: Collection of medical receipts, with a few cookery receipts: in English, written by several hands, but mostly by Mrs. Palmer. The date 1747 occurs on the second preliminary leaf, written by one of the later hands. A number of receipts are initialled S.P. and the name 'Sarah Palmer' appears in full on the 5th leaf from the end.

vga8q5cu.c: Collection of medical, cookery, household, and technical receipts: with notes and extracts on miscellaneous subjects, and additions by other hands. There are a number of inserted receipts, etc., including 14 in an envelope. These are by various hands, and of the first half of the 19th century. The latest dated entry is 'Lord Ponsonby's remedy for Cholera', with a cure for corns: these are signed 'W[illiam] R[obert] Ward 1868'. This would be presumably a relation of the original compiler, who was born in 1807 and died in 1879.

vhk9csuw.c: Physicall and chyrurgicall receipts. Cookery and preserves. The upper and lower covers are lettered 'Physick' and 'Cookery' respectively. Signature of 'Elizabeth Jacob' twice on the fourth leaf, and 'Eliz. Jacob 1654' on the fifth leaf. Though the beginnings of both sections are written by Elizabeth Jacob, there are many additions by other and later hands, especially by the writer of a neat upright script, which can perhaps be dated c. 1685.

vjc9jdyk.c: Accademia anatomico-fisiologica tenuta nella Camera Anatomica annessa allo Spedale di Camerino il di' 4 di April dell' anno 1802. Compiler's holograph MS. A collection of six 'Discorsi' on physiological subjects composed on the occasion of a visit to the Camerino Academy made by its Patron Monsignor Fabrizio Sceberras Testaferrata, Delegato Apostolico della Citta, e Ducato di Camerino, and dedicated to him. At the end is an 'Epilogo' in verse by Luigi Salusti of Camerino: there is also an 'Introduzione' in the form of a sonnet by Moreschini. This MS., which is written by the same hand throughout, was a copy probably prepared for publication, but no record of it has been traced in bibliographies. Produced in Camerino.

vk82cscx.c: Prescription notebook of a Nottinghamshire chemist, with medical, veterinary and household recipes and notes, The main part of the book (ff. 50-162) is occupied by prescriptions for named individuals from the northern fringes of Nottingham. At the start of the volume is a collection of recipes and medical notes (ff. 1-48). Most of the contents of both sections is apparently in a single hand.

vkpxmc3m.c: Collection of cookery receipts, including a few medical and household receipts: by several hands. The date 1800 is found on p. 6, and 1822 on p. 86.

vmafyazn.c: Manuscript book of culinary and medical recipes, in at least two hands and with signatures inside cover of Ann de la Bere and Hester de la Bere.54ff., contents as follows: f.1r: title page, "The Land of Promise Flowing With Milk & Hony....", relating to following scriptural material.f.1v: medical recipes.ff.2r-12v: scriptural material. ff.12v-40r: recipes, mixed culinary and medical.ff.40v-53r: recipes, mixed culinary and medical, written the other way up from the back of the book. ff.53v-54r: scribbles and handwriting experiments, including signatures of Ann de la Bere Hester de la Bere and Christian Rutter. f.54v: note on weights and measures.

vmwgbj99.c: Book of cookery receipts, with a few medical receipts. In English by two hands. The second hand (12 ll) is an illiterate one, and probably later. Inscribed inside the upper cover: 'Madm. Lettice Owen' [cf. following entry].

vpa6u8xf.t: 1 copy of Risālah fī al-falak by Yaḥyá ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb
vpa6u8xf.c: 1 copy of Risālah fī al-falak by Yaḥyá ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb

vpbfjwxq.c: Collection of cookery and medical receipts. With additional receipts by several hands. Some of the added receipts have been pasted in, or inserted loose. 'Elizabeth Fuller. 1712' is inscribed on the recto of the first leaf, within a pen-drawn circular decoration. The date 1822 is found in a scribbling on the title-page. Also includes a few inserted letters, one a love letter c.1805 enclosing a silhouette. Addressed to Sloane Family, Romsey, Hants.

vphnea7p.c: CABALE (La) magicochimique o? est d?couvert la Science des Cabalistes h?breux et des Philosophes herm?tiques. C'est ? dire la Connoissance du grand et petit monde. I.G.S.D.F.B. 1656. Illustrated with two full-page pen-drawings of the 'Astrological Man' and an 'Astrological Head', and several number and letter Tables and diagrams, of which four are folding. Text within red rules. A note by a later 18th cent. hand on the verso of the second fly-leaf states: 'Cet ouvrage n'a jamais ?t? imprim?, il a ?t? traduit du latin de G. G. Paris, par un c?l?bre alchymiste qui a pass? plus de 15 ann?es ? former ce recueuil [sic] pr?cieux pour les Enfants de l'art. Vendu format in 4to. ? la vente de M. Filhaut en 1779, 43l. 15s. Voyez Cailleau tome 3 page 259'.

vpnhsmb6.t: Lists of and notes on assorted Malay fish, medicinal roots, plants, animals, and growths.
vpnhsmb6.c: Lists of and notes on assorted Malay fish, medicinal roots, plants, animals, and growths.

vq9e75rz.c: Occulta scripta chymica.The content of the manuscript divides as follows: Pp.1-6: four psalms in German, and two Latin prayers. Pp.7-178 Secreta alchemica: in cipher, German. Pp.179-180: prayers in German. Pp.181-187: Elixir vitae: list of ingredients in Latin. Pp.188-209: alchemical and medicinal receipts, prayers, etc.: mainly in cipher, and in German, but "Virtutes olei" (pp.191-193) in Latin en clair. At the end "Scriptum Gottersdorff in meo exilio apud pastorem Severinum Drescherum Anno 1572".Pp.210-219: Ciment Regal: in German. Pp.221-252: Libellus de creatione omnium rerum Anno 1575 Die 23 Augusti. In der Naunburgk an der Sala. Authore Johanne Girlachio: in German. At the end "Anno Domini 1575 Die Jovis 25 Augusti". Lapis philosophorum. 1576 Die Saturni 25 February: in German. The end is wanting. Illustrated with numerous small water-colour symbolic alchemical drawings, some heightened with gold.Text within pen-drawn rules: some entries in red ink. Pp.1-178 are written entirely in cipher; pp.179-207 are partly in cipher and partly en clair; the remainder are en clair. Pp.253-321 and 335-350 are blank. The cipher consists of 51 symbols; a manuscript key to this, by Julius Koh

vqn45qvx.c: Collection of receipts and extracts on Brewing, Distillation of spirits, Wine-making, etc.: with numberous other technical receipts for varnishes, dyes, inks, etc. The date 1800 is found on p. 124.

vqw3gt9z.c: Collection of medical, cookery and household receipts: by several hands. The receipts are dated from 1802 (p. 17) to 1822 (p. 169): at the end, the 16 ll. contain pasted-down newspaper cuttings of miscellaneous receipts, dating from 1798 to 1823 and later.

vrxfa3nh.c: Miracle naturel, ou le grand Mist?re [sic] des Mist?res [sic] de la Nature, dans lequel on voit la Pierre magicochimique compos?e et perfectionn?e selon les vrais ?crits des vrais Philosophes choisis herm?tiques ce qui compose la M?decine Universelle. Illustrated with 24 full-page drawings and two half-page. Three of the full-page drawings are in sepia the rest in water-colour. The last full-page illustration is of alchemical apparatus, the others are symbolical of the Great Work. The last half-page drawing on p. 54 contains medallion portraits of the author and his wife Christina Leniau, with gold surround. Below these is the dedication: 'Josepho filio meo charissimo do, dico supradelineatas figuras hermeticas. Quibus facile intelliges magnum opus magisterii, si timeas deum, et semper orando, ac laborando, ne sis garrulus; sed pone ore tuo custodiam; Sacramentum Regis abscondere bonum est. Praecipue a magnatibus: propter gloriam Dei Jesus Christi et liberatatem tuam pretiosissimam. Vale et vive'. Following this is the text in Latin of the 'Miracle naturel' with a title, 'Miraculum naturale, seu mysterium enucleatum mysterium Naturae, veris dictis hermeticis philosophorum electis,

vs2ps9b2.t: Commentary on al-Qanun, the canon of Medicine, by Ibn Sina (Avicenna).
vs2ps9b2.c: Commentary on al-Qanun, the canon of Medicine, by Ibn Sina (Avicenna).

vs58jgv8.t: Astrological compendium based on the works of Ptolemy and others
vs58jgv8.c: Astrological compendium based on the works of Ptolemy and others

vsvqents.c: Book of cookery, medical, and domestic receipts. Inscribed on the outside upper cover 'W.B. 1785'.

vsyqmuam.c: Souverainet?s contre toutes maladies, tir?es et traduites de Marcellus, auteur ancien, par Anthione du Moulin, Masconnois. ? Lyon, par Jean de Tournes, 1550. Followed by: Dumontverd (Raoul) Choix des fleurs et secrets de m?decine ... traduites de latin en fran?ois ... Imprim?es nouvellement ? Paris, par Alain Lotrian et Denis Janot, 1531. Transcripts. The first work is a version of the author's 'De medicamentis', the editio princeps of which was published by Froben at Basle in 1536. The second work begins on p. 155, but is apparently unfinished.

vtwbaqav.c: Collection of veterinary receipts: in French. Mainly written by two hands. Inserted loose are 7 ll. containing fragments of a late 17th cent. work on veterinary medicine.

vtzjy5tp.t: Henry Daniel, Liber uricrisiarum, in English.
vtzjy5tp.c: Henry Daniel, Liber uricrisiarum, in EnglishWritten in an upright formal hand; 36 lines to a page. vuekysau.d: 6 Ramaḍān 1286  / 10 December 1869; 27 Ḏū l-Qa`da 1286 / 28 February 1870; 15 Ḏū l'Ḥiǧǧa 1286 / 18 March 1870
